sections.label: Budget long-term investment, surplus question
sections.summary: The Government is investing for the long term, with development expenditure rising faster than operating revenue and expenditure, despite a $15.1 billion surplus in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is therefore heartening that the Government is taking decisive steps to invest for the long term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We see this clearly in the Budget, with development expenditure rising faster than operating revenue and expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Some of my residents in Toa Payoh have asked me, "Why are there not more 'goodies', especially when we had a Budget surplus of $15.1 billion in 2025?" Mr Speaker, this is an understandable question.

sections.label: 2025 growth, US tariffs, volatility
sections.summary: Singapore's 2025 growth of 5% and higher corporate income tax from MNCs may not persist, with a 15% US global tariff and Middle East war risk adding volatility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While we performed better than expected in 2025, as our economy grew 5% beyond our expectations and multinational companies (MNCs) here did well and paid higher than expected corporate income tax, we cannot assume that such conditions will persist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In fact, latest developments in the past week out of the United States (US) with the new prevailing 15% global tariff and the risk of war in the Middle East adds to unanticipated volatility.

sections.label: Semiconductor, pharmaceutical tariff risk, windfall
sections.summary: Singapore still risks tariffs on its semiconductor and pharmaceutical sectors, so today's windfall should strengthen resilience rather than fund unsustainable spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For Singapore, there is still the risk of the semiconductor and pharmaceutical sectors being imposed tariffs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, it is therefore prudent that we channel today’s windfall towards strengthening resilience for tomorrow, rather than locking in spending that may not be sustainable.

sections.label: GST offsets, structural and temporary support
sections.summary: The Government provides transfer packages like GST offsets, enhanced schemes such as MediShield and the Jobseeker Relief Scheme, and Budget 2026 one-off support like CDC vouchers and utilities rebates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As we have seen over the past five years, the Government will not shy away from providing comprehensive transfer packages, such as the Goods and Services Tax (GST) offsets, to cushion the impact for Singaporeans and especially our lower-income households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Structurally, we have also enhanced schemes like MediShield, introduced the Jobseeker Relief Scheme and made the GST Voucher Scheme permanent, in order to give peace of mind to households who need help with their expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In addition to structural support, Budget 2026 continues the trend of providing one-off temporary support – in the form of the Cost-of-Living Special Payment, Community Development Council (CDC) vouchers and utilities rebates – when our fiscal position allows us to do so.

sections.label: Reviewing $20,000 income tax exemption
sections.summary: A phased adjustment to $25,000 or $30,000 would give relief, aid savings, and restore fairness, so the $20,000 exemption threshold should be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: A phased adjustment, for example, to $25,000 or $30,000, would: first, provide meaningful relief to lower- and middle-income groups; second, help them retain more savings and potentially asset-building; and third, restore structural fairness without undermining progressivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As our revenue mix has shifted more towards indirect taxes, it is reasonable to ensure that the lower-end of our income tax structure remains appropriately calibrated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, I hope the Ministry could consider reviewing whether the $20,000 exemption threshold remains aligned with its original purpose, given more than two decades of structural wage growth, higher reliance on indirect taxation and evolving cost of living realities.

sections.label: MRSS expansion, Silver Support thresholds
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the MRSS will be continued or expanded for family top-ups and whether Silver Support qualifying thresholds will be reviewed as seniors live longer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Will the MRSS be continued or even expanded to encourage family members and even husbands, to top up their elders' or homemaker wives' CPF balances and take advantage of dollar-for-dollar matching?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And whether the Government also review the Silver Support qualifying thresholds as our seniors live longer and deplete their earlier resources under their conditions currently?

sections.label: CPF life-cycle products terms
sections.summary: Asks whether new CPF life-cycle products will include automatic glide-path de-risking, fee caps and behavioural safeguards, and what terms of reference the CPF Board received.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The question I have is, will the new CPF life-cycle products include automatic glide-path de-risking, internationally benchmarked fee caps and behavioural safeguards, and what are the terms of reference that have already been given to the CPF Board?

sections.label: CPF retirement projections and refinement
sections.summary: Asks whether CPF can provide scenario-based projections including downside stress scenarios, and states the task is refinement for mobility and fairness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Among other things, it is no longer clear at what age an average Singaporean should retire and as human beings, we can never be sure how long more we will live after retirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: However, can CPF provide scenario-based projections, including downside stress scenarios, to strengthen confidence among Singaporeans that they can adequately provide for themselves after retirement?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Our task now is refinement – to ensure that our fiscal strength translates into sustained mobility for Singaporeans, for pushing for greater start-line equality, for broadening capital participation, calibrating fairness.

sections.label: Sectoral tariffs and fiscal surplus
sections.summary: States there has been little information on sectoral tariffs and their impact on Singapore, and that the PAP Government begins its term with a large fiscal surplus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Since then, however, there has been remarkably little information of the sectoral tariffs and their actual impact on Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Despite the doom and gloom surrounding the Liberation Day tariffs, this PAP Government begins its new term with what may be the greatest fiscal surplus any PAP Government has seen in decades.

sections.label: GDP growth and jobs
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister observed that GDP growth may no longer translate into jobs for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Deputy Prime Minister observed that GDP growth may no longer translate into jobs for Singapore.

sections.label: Ministerial bonus components questioned
sections.summary: Questions whether three of four national bonus components remain fit-for-purpose, whether under-employment is a fairer gauge, and whether GDP growth should stay in the formula.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Deputy Prime Minister Gan's remarks on GDP growth also call into question whether three of the four national bonus components, partly used to determine total Ministerial salaries, remain fit-for-purpose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Is the unemployment rate among Singaporeans still the right measure or has under-employment among Singaporeans become a more telling and fairer gauge to assess how much bonus Ministers ought to receive?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And if GDP growth will no longer reliably create good jobs for Singaporeans, should it remain in the Ministerial bonus formula at all?

sections.label: AI grant safeguards
sections.summary: Says clear standards must be set before AI-related grants and subsidies are paid, and that they must be ringfenced for transformative productivity gains to prevent gaming.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On AI-related subsidies through the Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG) and other initiatives, such as the Enterprise Innovation Scheme, clear standards and requirements must be established before grants and subsidies are paid out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: AI-related grants and subsidies must be ringfenced for truly transformative productivity gains, so that these taxpayers' subsidies are not gamed or abused.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singaporeans would remember the Productivity and Innovation Credit (PIC) scheme of yesteryear and how some individuals and businesses exploited it.

sections.label: RIE 2030 funding increase
sections.summary: Budget funds next RIE 2030 cycle at $37 billion, up from $25 billion for 2021 to 2025, with no comprehensive report on prior use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On that same note, this year's Budget revealed that the next cycle of the Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) 2030 plan stands to be funded to the tune of $37 billion, up from $25 billion in the previous cycle from 2021 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Yet, there was no comprehensive report on how the previous $25 billion was used, how many jobs were created for Singaporeans, where outcomes met their objectives, where they fell short or even whether it is simply too early to tell.

sections.label: Government fiscal surpluses
sections.summary: Government starts term with $15 billion FY2025 surplus, $8 billion expected FY2026, exceeding GST hike revenue estimates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On the fiscal position, the Government begins this term on a firm footing, with a surplus of $15 billion for FY2025, an $8 billion surplus expected for FY2026, with potentially more anticipated as corporate tax collections are expected to rise from FY2027.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These surpluses already far exceed the $2 billion to $3 billion or thereabouts, in additional revenue that the GST hikes of 2023 and 2024 were supposed to generate.

sections.label: Workers' top concerns survey
sections.summary: Survey ranks wages versus cost of living first at 37%, retirement savings second at 28%, job security third at 19%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The top concern cited by 37% of workers was wages not keeping up with the cost of living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The second was having enough savings for retirement, at 28%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Job security came in third at 19%, followed by caregiving demands at 9%, and concerns about AI disruption at 6%.

sections.label: US Supreme Court tariff ruling
sections.summary: The US Supreme Court struck down tariff measures, and a new 15% tariff was announced on all countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The US Supreme Court struck down the tariff measures and shortly thereafter, a new 15% tariff was announced on all countries, friends and foe alike.

sections.label: GST as structural revenue
sections.summary: GST is a long-term structural revenue source, and long-term responsibilities cannot be funded by short-term fortune.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Only then can we act effectively when the need arises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We must clarify a basic principle: GST is a long-term structural revenue source.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Long-term responsibilities cannot be funded by short-term fortune.

sections.label: Little Steps @ North West
sections.summary: Little Steps @ North West supports KidSTART families, giving children aged zero to six $500 annual support plus essentials with business partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In the North West District, we run Little Steps @ North West, supporting families participating in KidSTART.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Children aged zero to six receive $500 in annual support, with additional essentials provided in partnership with businesses.

sections.label: Middle powers and multilateral system
sections.summary: Singapore must strengthen ties with middle powers, uphold the multilateral system and defend rules under strain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Coming to the earlier topic, as great power rivalry intensifies and international law and trade rules come under strain, small and middle powers must cooperate more closely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Singapore has a responsibility to strengthen ties with other middle powers, uphold the multilateral system, and stabilise trade networks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: When rules are challenged, we must stand up to defend them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This too is part of the purpose of the Budget’s support for diplomacy and international engagement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Yet each time, we relied on two things: resilience and unity.

sections.label: Budget support for Singaporeans
sections.summary: The Budget supports young families, working adults, seniors and businesses in a range of ways.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Speaker, I support the Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This Budget covers a great many areas and as in previous years, supports Singaporeans in a range of thoughtful ways: providing support for young families who wish to have children, working adults who need support to get better jobs, seniors to have better healthcare and quality of life in their later years and businesses as they cope with a range of disruptions.

sections.label: Russia's invasion of Ukraine
sections.summary: Russia's invasion of Ukraine violates the UN Charter and the principle of territorial integrity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Russia’s invasion of Ukraine represents a clear violation of the United Nations (UN) Charter and the principle of territorial integrity.

sections.label: Tariffs and Venezuelan President capture
sections.summary: Last year's concern was tariffs on allies and competitors; this year the Venezuelan President's capture breached norms against use of force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The main concern last year was the imposition of tariffs on allies and competitors alike.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This year, the capture of the Venezuelan President was contrary to the peremptory norms against the use of force.

sections.label: Singapore's Free Trade Agreements
sections.summary: Singapore currently has 28 Free Trade Agreements spanning Asia, Europe and the Americas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As for economic trade, Singapore currently has 28 Free Trade Agreements spanning Asia, Europe and the Americas.

sections.label: UN Security Council geopolitical divisions
sections.summary: The UN Charter remains the framework for international peace and security, but the Security Council is hampered by geopolitical divisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Although the UN Charter remains the foundational framework for international peace and security, the UN Security Council has been hampered by geopolitical divisions.

sections.label: Smaller groupings and Digital Economy Agreements
sections.summary: Singapore has pioneered Digital Economy Agreements with trusted partners to set common rules on cross-border data flows, cybersecurity and digital trade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: While multilateral institutions remain essential, and we must continue to support them, smaller groupings of like-minded states can move faster and more pragmatically when progress stalls at the global levels through smaller agreements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For example, in the digital domain, Singapore has pioneered the Digital Economy Agreements with trusted partners to establish common rules on cross-border data flows, cybersecurity and digital trade.

sections.label: Strategic contest in new domains
sections.summary: Strategic contest between nations increasingly plays out in cyberspace, artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, space assets and critical infrastructure resilience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Strategic contest between nations increasingly play out in domains such as cyberspace, artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, space assets and the resilience of critical infrastructure.

sections.label: Cyber defence, digital resilience, AI governance
sections.summary: This Budget envisions strengthening cyber defence, enhancing digital resilience across public and private sectors, and building trusted AI governance frameworks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Strengthening cyber defence capabilities, enhancing digital resilience across both public and private sectors, and building trusted AI governance frameworks which will be essential and which is envisioned by this Budget.

sections.label: Singapore as trusted partner
sections.summary: Singapore maintains strong defence and economic ties with the US, engages constructively with China, and remains anchored in ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore has long cultivated a reputation as a consistent, honest and trusted partner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We maintain strong defence and economic ties with the US, engage constructively with China, and remain firmly anchored in ASEAN.

sections.label: Academic builds app with AI agents
sections.summary: A young academic volunteer hired somebody from Vietnam at $10 per hour and built an application using AI agents over a weekend.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: A young academic volunteer told me a story he wanted to build a simple application.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: He got a quote from a local IT service company for $70,000 to build the application.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: He got frustrated, hired somebody from Vietnam at $10 per hour and spent the weekend to build that same application using AI agents.

sections.label: AI Centres of Excellence here
sections.summary: Over 60 companies, including Google and Microsoft, have established AI Centres of Excellence in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Over 60 companies, including Google and Microsoft, have established AI Centres of Excellence here.

sections.label: Phased AI mandate for Government IT
sections.summary: Proposes a phased mandate requiring Government IT contracts to progressively adopt AI-centric development methods, with new projects first and legacy contracts given three-to-five-year transitions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Large companies have found it easier to continue with familiar methods while adding AI as a cosmetic layer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Therefore, I propose a phased mandate: Government IT contracts should progressively require AI-centric development methods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: New projects first, legacy contracts given longer runways and a clear three-to-five-year transition pathway.

sections.label: Onboarding AI-centric firms as PSG vendors
sections.summary: Hopes the Government will onboard AI-centric firms as PSG-approved vendors and co-fund transition costs so conventional SMEs can access them quickly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Over time, there will be a growing tier of AI-centric firms delivering accounting, payroll, marketing services or products.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: I hope the Government can consider actively onboarding these firms as PSG-approved vendors and co-fund the transition cost so that conventional SMEs can access them quickly.

sections.label: AI chance to re-invent economy
sections.summary: States that moving fast on AI-centric development in Government, IT services and SMEs gives a chance to re-invent the economy on hard-to-replicate foundations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: If we move fast enough, if we adopt AI-centric development in Government, bring our IT services industry with us and equip many layers of our SME industry, AI gives us the chance to not just manage our constraints but re-invent our economy on foundations that took decades to build, and that no competitor can replicate overnight.

sections.label: Funding for media against disinformation
sections.summary: Urges the Government to ensure media are adequately and sustainably funded and that media professionals find a compelling future in them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: In an age of AI-generated disinformation, they stand between our people and a manipulated information space.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to make sure that they are adequately and sustainably funded, and that our media professionals find a compelling future in them.

sections.label: Targeted housing programme for a group
sections.summary: Seeks a targeted programme for a group paying high rental rates, with features such as selective HDB loans, mortgage guarantees, a BTO pathway and long-term affordable rental.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: They are left paying high rental rates, with no clear pathways of getting their roof over their heads somewhere.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: I understand that this group have a lot of complexities and it is not due to any one source of difficulty that they face, but I hope the Government can consider a targeted programme, like how we invented Fresh Start for people in rental estate but the targeted programme helps this group that I mentioned with some of the following features: selective offering of HDB loans, Government-backed mortgage guarantees with maybe a bank like DBS, a structured pathway for BTOs where demonstrated income stability unlocks eligibility, or access to long-term affordable rental while they rebuild credit.

sections.label: Support for future forward Budget
sections.summary: Expresses full support for a future forward Budget, citing the Prime Minister's description of a revised FY2025 overall fiscal position with a $15.1 billion surplus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: In marked contrast, here in this Parliament, we are discussing a future forward Budget that not just responds to a changed world but also prepare ourselves to emerge stronger together in this AI-charged world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Therefore, Mr Speaker, this Budget deserves our full support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister describes our current fiscal position as fortunate, citing a revised FY2025 overall fiscal position that has resulted in a surplus of $15.1 billion.

sections.label: Retail food closures
sections.summary: More than 2,400 retail food establishments closed last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: More than 2,400 retail food establishments closed last year.

sections.label: Enterprise productivity contribution imbalance
sections.summary: ASME noted large enterprises contribute 74% of nominal value-added with 30% of workforce, while micro and small enterprises contribute 11% with 45%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: ASME pointed to a productivity and contribution imbalance: large enterprises contribute 74% of the nation's nominal value-added even though they employed just 30% of the national workforce; in contrast, micro and small enterprises contribute only 11% of the value-added despite employing 45% of the national workforce.

sections.label: Revised FY2025 surplus
sections.summary: The revised FY2025 surplus of $15.1 billion is more than double the original estimate of $6.81 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The revised FY2025 surplus of $15.1 billion is more than doubled the original estimate of $6.81 billion.

sections.label: GST hike re-evaluation question
sections.summary: With surpluses over $1 billion in all but one of the last five years, totalling $22 billion, the passage asks whether the GST hike's necessity should be re-evaluated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With surpluses of well over $1 billion in all but one of the last five years, totalling $22 billion, should we re-evaluate the necessity of the GST hike?

sections.label: AI expense tax deductions
sections.summary: The Government has allowed 400% tax deductions on AI expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government has also allowed 400% tax deductions on AI expenses.

sections.label: MTI development expenditure increase
sections.summary: MTI's development expenditures are estimated to double to $9.24 billion in FY2026, an increase of $4.32 billion in a single year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MTI's development expenditures is estimated to double to $9.24 billion in FY2026, which is an increase of $4.32 billion in a single year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For comparison, the entire development budget for the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) is a mere fraction of this, at just $260 million.

sections.label: Budget 2026 fiscal impulse
sections.summary: Budget 2026's fiscal impulse is only 0.6% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Yet, the fiscal impulse of Budget 2026 is only 0.6% of GDP.

sections.label: Cybersecurity budgets coverage question
sections.summary: A question asks whether this includes Government cybersecurity budgets, including Cyber Security Agency ones for critical information infrastructure protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can I ask if this includes the cybersecurity budgets across the Government, including those under the Cyber Security Agency for the protection of critical information infrastructure?

sections.label: Budget 2026 AI missions
sections.summary: Budget 2026 identifies four AI missions: finance, health, advanced manufacturing and connectivity, described as strategic growth pathways seen through trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Budget 2026 identifies four AI missions – finance, health, advanced manufacturing and connectivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Seen through the lens of trust, these missions are strategic growth pathways.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In finance, AI can position Singapore as the world's most trusted digital custodian enabling secure asset verification, counterparty validation and trusted trading ecosystems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In health, Singapore can be a trusted hub for clinical trials, diagnostics and genomic innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In advanced manufacturing, by anchoring intellectual property with trust, Singapore can embed itself in high value global supply chains.

sections.label: Avoiding near-term tax increases
sections.summary: Given the current surplus position, stability could be signalled by avoiding further tax increases in the near term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: At the same time, given the current surplus position, perhaps we can signal stability by avoiding further tax increases in the near term.

sections.label: AI job exposure estimates
sections.summary: The IMF estimates about 40% of jobs globally are exposed to AI, and Goldman Sachs estimates generative AI could affect 300 million full-time roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimates roughly 40% of jobs globally are exposed to AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Goldman Sachs estimates generative AI could affect work equivalent to 300 million full-time roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In the US, payroll growth was revised downward by over 400,000 jobs even as GDP grew 3.7% in the fourth quarter.

sections.label: Job-linked performance indicators question
sections.summary: A question asks what three to five key performance indicators, explicitly job linked, will be published annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What three to five key performance indicators will be published annually that are explicitly job linked?

sections.label: AI and entry-level pathways
sections.summary: Asks whether AI Mission partners will redesign entry-level pathways so young Singaporeans still get a real first job, mentorship and responsibility as AI takes over routine tasks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will AI Mission partners redesign entry-level pathways so that young Singaporeans still get a real first job, real mentorship and real responsibility, even as AI takes over routine tasks?

sections.label: Conditions on AI support
sections.summary: Asks whether AI support will be conditional on job redesign and wage progression commitments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will AI support be conditional on job redesign and wage progression commitments?

sections.label: AI Council speed-with-safety model
sections.summary: Asks what the AI Council's explicit speed-with-safety model is and whether the public sector will pair AI adoption with job redesign and publish measurable outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What is the AI Council’s explicit speed-with-safety model?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will the public sector pair AI adoption with systematic job redesign and publish measurable outcomes?

sections.label: Productivity, trust and mobility
sections.summary: States a future where productivity funds mobility and automation finances upgrading, not one where productivity rises but trust falls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Not a future where productivity rises but trust falls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: But a future where productivity funds mobility and automation finances upgrading.

sections.label: Budget surplus and fiscal outlook
sections.summary: Notes that this year's Budget Statement stood out for the sizeable expected FY2025 surplus and positive fiscal outlook in FY2026 and beyond.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As many have observed, what stood out in this year's Budget Statement is the sizeable surplus that the Government is expecting for FY2025, and the positive fiscal outlook in FY2026 and beyond.

sections.label: Reserves or earning capacity
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government should set the funds aside for a rainy day by replenishing reserves, or invest in infrastructure capabilities and human capital.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Should the Government set them aside for a rainy day by replenishing the reserves, earning financial returns in anticipation of future spending needs and exigencies, or should we invest in our earning capacity – in infrastructure capabilities and human capital?

sections.label: Addressing national gaps urgently
sections.summary: The nation must address gaps boldly and urgently, transcending existing policy paradigms, given challenges like living costs, wealth disparities, workforce disruption and population ageing.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As a nation, we need to address the gaps with boldness and urgency, and the willingness to transcend existing policy paradigms, because of the scale of the challenges we face, spanning the costs of living, wealth disparities, workforce disruption and population ageing.

sections.label: Budget focus on AI economy
sections.summary: Assurance and Togetherness underpin progress, and this year's Budget focuses on frontier technologies, notably building a competitive, AI-enabled economy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Assurance provides the confidence to navigate change and Togetherness sustains the trust that underpins our shared progress.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This year's Budget focuses on frontier technologies, notably how Singapore can build a competitive, AI-enabled economy.

sections.label: Support for firms using AI
sections.summary: Firms will receive support to use AI to transform their business through the new Champions of AI programme, the enhanced Enterprise Innovation Scheme and the PSG.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is important, not just at the national level but also for organisations and individuals.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am glad that firms will receive support to use AI to transform their business through the new Champions of AI programme and will also be able to tap the enhanced Enterprise Innovation Scheme and the PSG.

sections.label: Singapore as social investment state
sections.summary: Singapore is described as a social investment state, where social policy is geared towards education and skills development to enable people to earn a good living.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In sharing about Singapore's social policy with visitors, I often describe Singapore as a social investment state, where social policy is geared towards education and skills development to enable people to earn a good living.

sections.label: Liberalising Edusave and progressive accounts
sections.summary: Edusave use could be liberalised for non-school-based enrichment, with progressive Government contributions to Child Development or Edusave accounts and matched donor top-ups for less well-off children.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One possibility is to liberalise the use of Edusave to cover high-quality, non-school-based enrichment activities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To narrow the opportunity gap, the Government could provide children from lower-income families with additional support via the Child Development or Edusave accounts – in other words, make Government contributions to these accounts progressive.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Donors could also be encouraged to top up the accounts of less well-off children identified by schools or community organisations with matching funding from the Government in the spirit of a "we first" society.

sections.label: Remaining assurance gap for Singaporeans
sections.summary: Two decades of policy innovations strengthened social support and assurance, but more is needed because an assurance gap remains for many Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The past two decades have seen many groundbreaking policy innovations to strengthen social support and assurance, but we must go further because there is still an assurance gap for many Singaporeans.

sections.label: Value of vouchers and credits
sections.summary: The value of CDC vouchers, SG60 vouchers and LifeSG credits announced in last year's Budget amounted to over $3 billion.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If I am not wrong, the value of CDC vouchers, SG60 vouchers and LifeSG credits announced in last year's Budget amounted to over $3 billion.

sections.label: Vouchers as social dividend
sections.summary: The vouchers and credits could be repositioned as a social dividend, an annual sum given to citizens signifying a stake in the country and its collective wealth.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The vouchers and credits could be repositioned as a social dividend, an annual sum given to citizens that signifies that they have a stake in the country and its collective wealth.

sections.label: Income-generating assets for low-income households
sections.summary: The second suggestion is to give low-income households part of the social dividend in income-generating assets and securities, beyond cash and vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The second suggestion is to give low-income households part of the social dividend in income-generating assets and securities, beyond just cash and vouchers.

sections.label: Tracking essential goods affordability
sections.summary: Affordability indicators exist for public housing and healthcare, and the percentage of households whose expenditure on food, utilities and other essentials exceeds a proportion of income could likewise be tracked.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are already affordability indicators for public housing, such as the ratio of new flat prices to incomes; and for healthcare, the share of out-of-pocket expenditure in total health spending.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We could likewise track the percentage of households whose expenditure on food, utilities and other essential goods and services exceeds a certain proportion of their income.

sections.label: Net strength of hypothetical country
sections.summary: The net strength of this hypothetical country would be two-thirds minus one-third, but if united it is two-thirds plus one-third, or perhaps more than the sum of its parts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The net strength of this hypothetical country would be two-thirds minus one-third, but if the country is united, then it is two-thirds plus one-third, or perhaps even more than the sum of its parts.

sections.label: Caring, relating and equipping future generations
sections.summary: What matters most is how we care for the vulnerable, relate to people with different views and equip future generations, with success depending on collective actions of citizens and stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Ultimately, what matters most is how we care for the vulnerable among us, how we relate to people whose views are different from ours and how we equip future generations with confidence and opportunity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Success will depend not only on policies and spending, but on the collective actions of citizens and stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If together, we can achieve the FEAT of future readiness, empowerment, assurance and togetherness, I believe Singapore will continue to flourish as a resilient, cohesive and exceptional nation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In my view, this Budget is a step forward in this direction, though we have much further to go.

sections.label: Reshaping parents' lived experiences
sections.summary: The passage states that encouraging parenthood requires reshaping the lived experiences of parents or potential parents, which shapes perceptions of support given.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, if we are serious about encouraging parenthood, we must reshape the lived experiences of parents or potential parents, which shapes perceptions of support given.

sections.label: Singapore TFR 2024
sections.summary: The passage states that Singapore's TFR in 2024 remains at a historical low of 0.97.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Our TFR in 2024 remains at a historical low of 0.97.

sections.label: Jumbo BTO flats idea
sections.summary: The passage describes an idea for a 'room to grow' flat mimicking larger HDB units, designed for modern family needs including those relying on domestic helpers.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: One idea is they can select a "room to grow" flat, where it mimics a larger format of HDB units, in what I may call "jumbo BTO flats", and these are thoughtfully designed for modern family needs where some of our families rely on domestic helpers.

sections.label: Eligibility linked to children
sections.summary: The passage states eligibility to apply for such units could be linked to couples committing to have two or more children within five to seven years of MOP.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For example, eligibility to apply for such units could be linked to couples committing to have two or more children within the first five to seven years of Minimum Occupation Period (MOP) after key collection.

sections.label: MOP changes and priority
sections.summary: The passage states ideas include reducing or suspending MOP for couples expecting or having children, and resetting eligibility for larger BTOs with higher priority.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For instance, reducing or suspending MOP if couples are expecting or have additional children during that period; and even concurrently "resetting" their eligibility to apply for larger BTOs and for them to accord higher priority in the application process.

sections.label: Childcare leave days
sections.summary: The passage states parents get six days paid childcare leave per child when the child is six or younger, and two days extended leave for ages seven to twelve.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Today, parents get six days of paid childcare leave, per child, when their child is six years old or younger, but only two days of extended childcare leave when the child is between seven to twelve.

sections.label: Childcare leave flexibility redesign
sections.summary: Suggests keeping childcare leave capped at six days per parent but allowing flexible use across a wider age band or a gradual taper from seven to two, and studying a higher cap for parents with more children.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For example, instead of a sharp step-down in leave provisions once a child turns seven, we could keep the overall number of childcare leave capped at six days per parent, but allow families to use this portion of their leave flexibly across a wider age band or redesigning the entitlement so it tapers off gradually, instead of a sharp drop, from seven to two.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We should also study whether parents with more children should have a modestly higher cap.

sections.label: Dual-Use Scheme expansion
sections.summary: Welcomes the expansion of the Dual-Use Scheme so families can access school facilities conveniently.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: On this note, I also want to say that I welcome the expansion of the Dual-Use Scheme so that families can access school facilities conveniently.

sections.label: Awareness as policy lever
sections.summary: Says awareness should be treated as a policy lever and hopes the new statutory board from the WSG and SSG merger will reach out to students and workers without strong industry networks.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: So, beyond simply just redesigning a website, we should treat awareness as a policy lever.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I hope the new statutory board of the merger between WSG and SSG will reach out to students and workers without strong industry networks.

sections.label: Means-tested Curiosity Credits idea
sections.summary: Recalls saying aspirations are shaped by experience and experience by access, and mentions the idea of means-tested Curiosity Credits so every child has a budget to discover interests and strengths.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I have said in my maiden speech that aspirations are shaped by experience, and experiences are shaped by access.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: That is why, previously, I have mentioned the idea of a means-tested "Curiosity Credits," which is a simple idea that regardless of any family background, every child should have the budget to be able to allow them to discover their interests and strengths by having the opportunity to try things, like songwriting, playing a musical instrument, robotics, sports – and the list goes on.

sections.label: SkillsFuture taster courses and meritocracy
sections.summary: Suggests SkillsFuture consider low-cost or subsidised taster lessons, courses and micro-attachments in new industries, and says Singapore should stay anchored in meritocracy while recognising it may compound advantages across generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: SkillsFuture can consider creating a low-cost or subsidised "taster" lessons or courses and micro-attachments in new industries, so Singaporeans can experience the nature of the work before committing time and money into a full course.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: At this point, I just want to take a step back and submit that we should, as a country, continue to be anchored in meritocracy.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: But we also must be hard-nosed in recognising that meritocracy, over time, may also accumulate and compound advantages across generations.

sections.label: Whole-of-Government approach needed
sections.summary: Argues a central agency is needed to set overarching objectives, deliberate trade-offs and compel design, and asks for a sharper willingness to reshape lived experience through a whole-of-Government approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Because transport agencies will rightly push for a car-lite vision; housing agencies will manage land scarcity and affordability; and fiscal agencies will rightly guard anything against these benefits becoming permanent.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: That is why we need a whole-of-Government approach only when there is a central agency that sets an overarching objective, deliberate trade-offs, compel design and serve system-wide goals.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: When system runs coherently, residents experience less friction.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: But the trends we face, especially on fertility and the risk of widening opportunity gaps, I ask for something more: a sharper willingness to reshape lived experience through whole-of-Government approach, not just in flagship policies, but also in the everyday systems that determines friction, time and stress in residents' lives.

sections.label: Singapore R&D funding plans
sections.summary: Singapore spent about $25 billion on five-yearly science and technology plans from 1991 to 2010, and RIE 2030 is allocated $37 billion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore rolled out its five-yearly science and technology plans from 1991 to 2010, spending about $25 billion over the years to build up our R&D capabilities, infrastructure and manpower.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This year, 2026 to 2030, or what we call the RIE 2030, is allocated $37 billion.

sections.label: Singapore innovation input output ranking
sections.summary: Singapore is ranked fifth in 2025 for innovation input and ninth for innovation output such as licensings and trademarks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For Singapore, what is our ranking in 2025?

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We are ranked number five and that sounds very good, right?

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, innovation input is on infrastructure, the Government actions, especially the R&D dollars.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But innovation output – which is the licensings, the trademarks and all the other IPs that we file for commercialisation, we are number nine.

sections.label: Companies from first phase
sections.summary: During the first phase, about 250 companies were churned out.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: During the first phase, we had churned out a lot of companies, about 250 of them.

sections.label: Special listing rules for technology ventures
sections.summary: MetaOptics skipped Series A funding and went directly to an IPO on Catalist, cited as a pilot for special listing rules for technology ventures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MetaOptics skipped Series A funding and goes directly to an initial public offering (IPO) on Catalist.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And the Minister of State Dinesh was there to witness, with the gong.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, we use this as a reference or the pilot point for us to say, "Hey, why not we create a special path for technology ventures?" Special listing rules for technology ventures that allow them, with criteria listed by the exchange, the sponsors and maybe a group of wise old men, meaning people who have done technology ventures before, to determine whether they are suitable for such acceleration programme, fast track, or we can call it, in Singapore style, through-train.

sections.label: HKEX specialist technology pathway
sections.summary: The Hong Kong Stock Exchange already has a special pathway for specialist technology companies, but of a bigger scale.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If you look at the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, the HKEX already has a special pathway for specialist technology companies, but this is of a bigger scale.

sections.label: Foster families and foster kids
sections.summary: In late 2024 there are 600 foster families, and the speaker has three foster kids at home.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In late 2024, we have 600 foster families and currently, in my house I have three foster kids.

sections.label: Free childcare for first-born
sections.summary: A suggestion is made to consider free childcare and infant care for the first-born.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Maybe we should consider for the first-born, we have free childcare and infant care.

sections.label: Revenue pillars: taxes and NIRC
sections.summary: Revenue rests mainly on taxes and statutory collections, and Net Investment Returns Contributions, which are not unlimited.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Today, our revenue rests mainly on two pillars: taxes and statutory collections, and our Net Investment Returns Contributions (NIRC).

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: These two revenue taps have served us well but they are not unlimited.

sections.label: Singapore competitiveness and innovation ranking
sections.summary: Singapore is the second most competitive and fifth most innovative economy globally.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Today, Singapore is the second most competitive and the fifth most innovative economy globally.

sections.label: TSMC valuation and Taiwanese Government returns
sections.summary: TSMC is the world's second most valuable semiconductor company, with the Taiwanese Government as biggest shareholder receiving over one billion dollars annually.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Today, it is the world’s second most valuable semiconductor company with a valuation about three times the size of Singapore’s GDP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Taiwanese Government remains the single biggest shareholder and TSMC returns more than one billion dollars annually to the Taiwanese Government.

sections.label: DSA scheme as uneven battleground
sections.summary: The DSA scheme is an uneven battleground where parental resources give some an advantage over less privileged peers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: What this all means is the DSA scheme is now just an uneven battleground in the education arms race, where those with the advantage of parental resources enjoy a leg up over their less privileged peers.

sections.label: Feedback on DSA and affiliated admissions
sections.summary: Feedback said some popular schools had few places left after DSA and affiliated admissions, with some children balloted out despite meeting cut-off points.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: These were motivated by direct feedback from the ground.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I heard that some popular brand name schools only had a few places left after DSA and affiliated admissions, and the children who had made the cut-off points at some of these schools had to fight for a small number of remaining places.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Some were balloted out despite meeting the even more stringent cut-off points for non-affiliated students.

sections.label: Quota for non-affiliated students
sections.summary: A suggestion was made for MOE to consider a separate hard quota for non-affiliated and non-DSA students, which MOE will study.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: One of the suggestions I made to the Ministry of Education (MOE) in my supplementary question was to ask MOE to consider setting aside a separate, hard quota for non-affiliated and non-DSA students.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This will preserve an open pathway to some popular schools for them and I think it will be at least a good interim measure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I am glad to note that MOE will study my suggestion and that the Ministry is taking a look at the DSA scheme as part of a more comprehensive review.

sections.label: Fertility, wages and business costs
sections.summary: Singapore's fertility rate is around 0.97, median age exceeds 42, wage growth outpaced productivity, and the business community welcomes cost-mitigation measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At home, Singapore's total fertility rate remains around 0.97, our median age exceeds 42, labour force growth will slow structurally over the coming decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the same time, remuneration per worker rose by about 3.4%, with wage growth outpacing productivity in several labour-intensive domestic sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The business community welcome the measures to mitigate rising business costs – including the 40% Corporate Income Tax rebate, expanded internationalisation support, enhanced enterprise financing and the expansion of the PSG.

sections.label: National AI Council
sections.summary: The Prime Minister will chair a new National AI Council, and specific sectors have been identified for coordinated AI transformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister will chair a new National AI Council to drive the agenda, and specific sectors have been identified for coordinated AI transformation.

sections.label: Budget 2026 AI support
sections.summary: Budget 2026 seeks to change the risk equation through the Champions of AI programme, expanded EIS for AI expenditure and broader PSG support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Through the Champions of AI programme, expanded Enterprise Innovation Scheme (EIS) for AI expenditure and broader PSG support, Budget 2026 seeks to change the risk equation.

sections.label: Risk-sharing for overseas expansion
sections.summary: The Government enhanced internationalisation support, but asks whether risk-sharing mechanisms could be calibrated by market risk for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government has taken important steps: enhanced Market Readiness Assistance support of up to 70% for SMEs, the raised Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation cap to $400,000 and expanded Enterprise Financing Scheme limits materially reduce the financial burden of overseas expansion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For companies prepared to reposition and compete regionally or globally, these measures are helpful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, emerging markets across Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Africa and Latin America offer growth, but they also carry higher political, regulatory and receivables risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While existing financing schemes provide access to capital, the binding constraint for many SMEs is working capital resilience in higher-risk markets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Would the Government therefore consider calibrating risk-sharing mechanisms more explicitly by market risk, for example, enhanced trade credit coverage or working capital guarantees in markets where the opportunity is real, but the uncertainty deters participation?

sections.label: Consortium bids and regional fluency
sections.summary: Schemes could be adapted to incentivise consortium-led bids, and Singapore must strengthen market intelligence and in-market advisory platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Schemes, such as the Market Readiness Assistance and Enterprise Financing schemes, could be adapted to provide explicit incentives for consortium-led bids, enabling firms to "hunt as a pack" and pool complementary strengths to pursue opportunities that no single company could realistically secure alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And as firms from Northeast Asia and Europe increasingly view Singapore as a gateway into Southeast Asia, we must ask whether our ecosystem has sufficient regional fluency, multilingual advisory capability, regulatory expertise, deep local partnerships, to anchor these flows here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we want to capture these investment and trade flows, we must strengthen not just financing, but market intelligence and in-market advisory platforms, working closely with trade associations and chambers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is to force your opponent to make one." Budget 2026 recognises that Singapore cannot afford to wait, especially in an increasingly uncertain and volatile world.

sections.label: Taking the offensive with discipline
sections.summary: The passage states that in a structurally tighter Singapore, taking the offensive with discipline and conviction means not merely responding to structural change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a structurally tighter Singapore, hesitation is not caution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we take the offensive with discipline and conviction, we will not merely respond to structural change.

sections.label: Origins of iconic childhood bowls
sections.summary: The passage states these iconic childhood bowls were not made in Singapore but designed by Hakka and Teochew craftsmen in Guangdong and produced in China and Thailand in the 1950s.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: These bowls, so iconic to our childhoods, were not made in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: They were designed by Hakka and Teochews craftsmen in Guangdong and produced in places like Chaoshan in China and Lampang in Thailand, in the 1950s.

sections.label: Dragon jars and their names
sections.summary: The passage states the massive ceramic water jars in bathrooms and kitchens before modern plumbing were called Leng An, Giam Chai Ang or Geng.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: You could make the dragon jars, People call it "Leng An”, “Giam Chai Ang” or “Geng” the massive ceramic water jars that sat in our bathrooms and kitchens before modern plumbing.

sections.label: Earth colour at construction sites
sections.summary: The passage states that earth turned over at a construction site in Jurong or Redhill is not brown.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: If you have ever seen the earth turned over at a construction site in Jurong or at Redhill, you will notice it is not brown.

sections.label: Ceramist and director family project
sections.summary: The passage states ceramist Kim Whye Kee made 100 ceramic bowls with the pomfret motif and director Royston Tan filmed 100 dinners with 100 families.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: Recently, I was moved by a project by our renowned local ceramist Kim Whye Kee who made 100 such ceramic bowls with the pomfret motif and our famous film director Royston Tan who filmed 100 dinners with 100 families.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: Through their lens, we see the joys, the struggles of each family, each diverse, different phases in life.

sections.label: Prudence, dragon jar, three kia
sections.summary: The passage states COVID-19 was met by drawing on 20 years of surpluses, and names three kia that make Singapore successful.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: Because of that, when COVID-19 struck, we were able to draw on 20 years of surpluses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: That prudence, that stewardship, that iron-will to save for a rainy day, that is the dragon jar of our nation that held water when the well ran dry.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: So, why am I telling you about clay and jars and bowls and family dinners?

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: I think of the three "kia" that make Singapore successful: "kiasu" (怕输), the fear of losing, which drives us to prepare; "kiasi" (怕死), the fear of death, which makes us value safety, life and respect for others; and "kiabo" (怕没) the fear of not having enough, which drives us to work hard and save for the future.

sections.label: Pioneering spirit and unity
sections.summary: It warns against a frivolous culture and urges developing abilities, keeping the pioneering spirit and remaining united.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: It is a stark reminder for our current and future generations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: We fear our worst fate is to drift into a culture that is frivolous, thinking that we have arrived with easy effort.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: Even with a rich inheritance, we must develop our own abilities and keep the pioneering spirit alive, and to remain united against all odds, however complex the external environment may be.

sections.label: AI tools and workload
sections.summary: AI adoption failed to reduce workload, making employees busier and risking job intensification and workplace burn-out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The adoption of AI tools has not only failed to reduce the employees' workload, but made them busier instead.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is because the adoption of AI tools has accelerated the pace of work, expanded their scope of work and lengthened their working hours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The risk is not merely that AI eliminates some jobs, but that it leads to job intensification, resulting in workplace burn-out.

sections.label: Marriage and Parenthood Survey
sections.summary: The 2021 survey shows over 90% of married Singaporeans want two or more children, but over half have one or none.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The 2021 Marriage and Parenthood Survey results shows that while over 90% of married Singaporeans want to have two or more children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In reality however, more than half only have one child or none at all.

sections.label: AI reliance and work density
sections.summary: AI adoption did not reduce workload, instead accelerating tasks, deepening reliance and increasing work density and volume.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The adoption of AI tools did not reduce workload.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: AI accelerated tasks, which raised the expectation for speed, which deepened reliance on AI, which expanded the scope of work, which further increased the density and volume of work for each employee.

sections.label: Singapore working week hours
sections.summary: Singapore's average full-time working week is nearly 44 hours, excluding unpaid overtime work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Singapore's average full-time working week stands at nearly 44 hours, not including unpaid overtime work.

sections.label: Burn-out economic cost
sections.summary: Burn-out costs the Singapore economy an estimated $15.7 billion annually in lost productivity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Burn-out costs the Singapore economy an estimated $15.7 billion annually in lost productivity.

sections.label: Falling total fertility rate
sections.summary: Singapore's total fertility rate has fallen below one and held at 0.97 since 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Our TFR has since plunged below one, holding steady at 0.97 since 2023.

sections.label: Private tuition spending rise
sections.summary: Singaporean families spent $1.8 billion on private tuition in 2023, up 64% from a decade ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Singaporean families collectively spent $1.8 billion on private tuition in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is up 64% from a decade ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It is a rational response to a system that sorts early and sorts sharply.

sections.label: WSG and SSG merger board
sections.summary: The passage welcomes a new Statutory Board from merging WSG and SSG and hopes it builds career frameworks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It reflects the very qualities we say we want in our workforce – adaptability, entrepreneurial thinking and a willingness to take calculated risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I look forward to hearing more about the mandate of the new Statutory Board formed by the merger of WSG and SSG.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I hope it will build complementary and updated frameworks for career development and ensure labour protection and skill certification to accommodate diverse work arrangements, while safeguarding longer-term income security and career progression.

sections.label: Economic growth and headwinds
sections.summary: The economy grew 5% last year, but projected 2% to 4% growth this year reflects persistent external headwinds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Last year, our economy grew by 5%, which gives us confidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But this year's projected growth of 2% to 4% reminds us that external headwinds are real and likely to persist.

sections.label: Support for older workers
sections.summary: CPF top-ups, the Long-Term Care Support Fund, and employment schemes strengthen retirement adequacy and older worker retention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: CPF top-ups and higher contribution rates strengthen retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Long-Term Care Support Fund reinforces CareShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Senior Employment Credit and the Tripartite Workgroup on Senior Employment encourage businesses to continue hiring and retaining older workers.

sections.label: AI strategy principles in Budget
sections.summary: Three AI principles proposed in Budget 2024 debate appear reflected in Budget 2026 measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the Budget 2024 debate, I proposed three principles: first, AI strategy must be driven from the centre with direct oversight from the Prime Minister; second, we should focus on high value, sector-specific deployments, at scale; and third, that trust and governance will be our differentiator in a world racing ahead with AI.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I am encouraged to see these principles reflected in Budget 2026: in the National AI Council chaired by the Prime Minister; in the AI Missions across advanced manufacturing, connectivity, healthcare and finance; and in the stronger enterprise incentives including the Champions of AI and SME grants, and the emphasis on deeper AI literacy, governance and responsible deployment.

sections.label: Agentic AI value share growth
sections.summary: The firm estimates Agentic AI will double its share of AI-driven value creation from 17% today to 29% by 2028, outpacing traditional AI and GenAI.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: By 2028, my firm estimates that Agentic AI will double its share of AI-driven value creation, from 17% today to 29%, outpacing traditional AI and GenAI.

sections.label: Value captured elsewhere
sections.summary: If core systems and standards are designed elsewhere, Singapore may use AI extensively but see much of the value captured elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If the core systems are all designed elsewhere, the standards are all written elsewhere, we may use AI extensively, but see much of the value be captured elsewhere.

sections.label: Jobs and wages determine progress
sections.summary: Vouchers help families cope with this year's prices, but jobs and wages determine whether families truly get ahead in the years ahead.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: They help families cope with this year's prices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But what determines whether families truly get ahead, in the years ahead, is not vouchers, but jobs and wages.

sections.label: Exportable RegTech agents
sections.summary: Exportable RegTech agents embed Singapore's transparent, rules-based, trusted regulatory philosophy, cementing its position as a global finance hub.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Exportable "RegTech agents" that embed Singapore's regulatory philosophy – transparent, rules based, trusted – cementing our position as a global finance hub.

sections.label: Multi-year support for AI Champions
sections.summary: Support and financial backing for AI Champions must be structured and multi-year, tied to measurable productivity outcomes and anchored by CEO and Board leadership.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If we expect our Champions of AI to redesign operating models over multiple years, then support and financial backing must also be structured and multi-year, tied to measurable productivity outcomes and anchored by accountable leadership at the chief executive officer (CEO) and Board level.

sections.label: Teaching Singaporeans to think with AI
sections.summary: Singaporeans must be taught not just to use AI but to think with, challenge and govern it, through reskilling, certifications, mentorship and applied learning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, we must teach Singaporeans not just how to use AI but how to think with AI, to challenge it and to govern it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This means serious investments in mid-career reskilling and professional certifications in AI supervision and AI operations, mentorship and applied learning and building a culture of collaboration with AI.

sections.label: AI literacy and apprenticeships
sections.summary: The passage proposes mandatory AI literacy modules, structured apprenticeships and externships, and curricula developing critical thinking, problem-solving, functional skills, ethics, systems thinking and domain knowledge.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Mandatory AI literacy modules across Institutes of Technical Education, polytechnics and universities, structured apprenticeships and externships when they are still in school, when they work directly alongside seasoned professionals and AI systems and curricula that develop critical thinking, problem-solving, functional skills, ethics, systems thinking and domain knowledge necessary to progress quickly into mid-level roles.

sections.label: ComLink+ AI Capability Milestones
sections.summary: The passage proposes introducing AI Capability Milestones for ComLink+ families, such as parents completing AI literacy modules, children using AI safely for schoolwork, and families setting up supervised AI tools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Today, ComLink+ supports families with goals around employment and education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We can introduce AI Capability Milestones, such as when the parent completes foundational AI literacy module; when a child demonstrates safe and effective use of AI for schoolwork; or when a family sets up supervised AI tools for job search or for their home-based business.

sections.label: Tracking AI outcomes and displacement
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government will commit to tracking and releasing annual value creation, productivity and wage uplift outcomes from AI adoption alongside data on jobs displaced by AI.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As we pursue this agenda, will the Government commit to tracking and releasing annual value creation, productivity and wage uplift outcomes attributable to AI adoption across key sectors alongside data on jobs displaced by AI?
