sections.label: Agentic AI and Singapore's future
sections.summary: The passage states that if done right, agentic AI will not replace Singaporeans, and that multiplication is how Singapore remains sovereign, competitive and extraordinary, with orchestrators shaping the future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If we get this right, agentic AI will not replace Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For a small nation, multiplication is not optional.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It is how we remain sovereign, how we remain competitive, how we remain extraordinary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the age of agentic AI, those who orchestrate will shape the future.

sections.label: National AI Council and missions
sections.summary: The passage states that the Prime Minister announced a National AI Council and sector-specific AI missions, signalling intent for Government-supported AI application in key sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister's announcement of the formation of a National AI Council and the launch of sector-specific AI missions signal a clear intent to move toward Government-supported application of AI in sectors that are key to Singapore's economy and society.

sections.label: AI adoption versus efficiency gains
sections.summary: The passage states that while the Government introduced the Green Data Centre Road Map, the current pace of AI adoption may risk outstripping efficiency gains.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While the Government has introduced the Green Data Centre Road Map, the current pace of AI adoption may risk outstripping our efficiency gains.

sections.label: Data centre efficiency and AI models
sections.summary: The DC-CFA2 sets a PUE target of 1.25 and requires software-level accountability so government-funded AI solutions prioritise small, task-specific models.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Alongside infrastructure, efficiency standards, like the power usage effectiveness (PUE) target of 1.25 in the Infocomm Media Development Authority's (IMDA's) latest Data Centre – Call for Application (DC-CFA2), which will also require software level accountability ensuring that the AI Solutions receiving Government funding, including those under the enhanced Enterprise Innovation Scheme prioritise small AI and task-specific models that require a fraction of the energy of general purpose large language models (LLMs).

sections.label: Ireland data centre grid requirements
sections.summary: Ireland requires data centres to have 100% on-site backup capacity and 80% renewable matching, while DC-CFA2 targets only 50% green energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While Ireland requires data centres to be active partners in grid reliability through 100% on-site, backup capacity and 80% renewable matching, our current DC-CFA2 framework only targets 50% green energy, leaving a significant gap that our national grid and, by extension, the ordinary taxpayer must bridge.

sections.label: National AI Council and energy disclosures
sections.summary: The National AI Council must bridge digital ambition and environmental reality, with a regulatory framework mandating energy disclosures for large-scale AI developers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: If we are to achieve our net-zero 2050 commitments, the National AI Council must bridge the gap between digital ambition and environmental reality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We need a clear regulatory framework that mandates energy disclosures for large-scale AI developers, like the European Union (EU) which will begin mandating energy disclosures for large AI developers by August this year.

sections.label: ExxonMobil retrenchment and just transition fund
sections.summary: ExxonMobil will retrench up to 500 Singapore workers by 2027, prompting a call for a dedicated just transition fund for affected petrochemical workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In October 2025, ExxonMobil announced it would retrench up to 500 workers in Singapore by 2027.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: What specific retraining support is being provided to these hundreds of workers affected by such structural shifts?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: If we can find $500 million to finance regional green infrastructure via the Financing Asia's Transition Partnership fund, I am sure we can also find the resources to ensure no Singaporean worker is left behind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I call for the establishment of a dedicated just transition fund to assist, not just the 500 workers laid off, but to help all workers in the petrochemical industry in the coming years who may be affected as we transition away from fossil fuels, including providing specific guidance in transiting to different industry or jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Prime Minister announced in his Budget speech that Preferential Additional Registration Fee (PARF) rebates have now been lowered by 45% across the board and the maximum rebate has been reduced from $60,000 to $30,000.

sections.label: Heavy Vehicles Zero Emissions Scheme incentive
sections.summary: The $40,000 Heavy Vehicles Zero Emissions Scheme incentive launched on 1 January 2026 may remain under-utilised without faster hydrogen pilots or battery swap licences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Furthermore, the $40,000 incentive under the Heavy Vehicles Zero Emissions Scheme, launched on 1 January 2026 may remain under-utilised unless we can move faster on shortlisted hydrogen pilots or permanent battery swap licences to support our delivery community and logistics sector.

sections.label: Subsidy gap for complex dental cases
sections.summary: Patients referred to tertiary institutions for complicated dental procedures are ineligible for the same Pioneer Generation CHAS subsidies received at polyclinics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the higher subsidies and MediSave use for tooth saving treatments, we must address the subsidy gap for complex cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Currently, patients referred to tertiary institutions, like the National Dental Centre for complicated procedures, often due to pre-existing frailty, find themselves ineligible for the same Pioneer Generation CHAS subsidies they will receive at the polyclinic.

sections.label: Dental subsidies and IP riders
sections.summary: A speaker urges harmonising PG and CHAS dental subsidies, noting from April 2026 new IP riders will not cover deductibles and co-payment caps rise $6,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: But she was denied PG or CHAS subsidies for the procedure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to harmonise these subsidies so that our seniors are not financially, penalised because their dental-related medical needs require a hospital setting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: From April 2026, new Integrated Plan (IP) riders will no longer cover deductibles and co-payment caps will rise $6,000.

sections.label: CPF excess funds for premiums
sections.summary: A speaker asks whether the CPF Board will let members who meet the Basic Healthcare Sum retain excess funds for annual insurance premiums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While this boosts monthly payout, it does not help with the lump sum nature of annual insurance premiums which can reach several thousand dollars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Therefore, will the CPF Board consider allowing CPF members who have me their Basic Healthcare Sum to retain a portion of excess funds in their Ordinary Account or a dedicated insurance sub-account.

sections.label: Four areas and disability support
sections.summary: A speaker considers four areas and welcomes Budget support for persons with disabilities, including the Long-Term Care Support Fund top-up and DAC expansion.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I will consider this across four areas: firstly, persons with disabilities and their caregivers; secondly, vulnerable young children; thirdly, youth development and fourthly, families navigating complex needs.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I welcome the continued support in this Budget for persons with disabilities and their caregivers, including the top-up to the Long-Term Care Support Fund and the planned expansion of Day Activity Centre (DAC) capacity.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For many families, one of the most significant transitions occurs when their child exits the formal education system at about 18 years of age.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This transition often entails a loss of structured routines, peer networks and community participation, while families navigate a new landscape of adult services.

sections.label: Preschool affordability and access
sections.summary: The Budget continues to strengthen affordability and access to the preschool sector, described as steps to ensure no child is left behind.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Budget continues to strengthen affordability and access to the preschool sector, and these are important steps at ensuring no child is left behind.

sections.label: Youth development investments
sections.summary: On youth development, the Budget makes investments in traineeships, skills development and employment pathways.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On youth development, this Budget makes important investments in traineeships, skills development and employment pathways.

sections.label: Families as partners in transitions
sections.summary: A speaker says policies empowering families as partners in navigating institutional supports can sustain participation and reduce discontinuities between transitions.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Families often serve as primary coordinators across education, employment, healthcare and community systems, particularly during transitions, such as school-to-work or caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Policies that empower families, not only as recipients of services, but as partners in navigating institutional supports can help sustain participation and reduce discontinuities between transitions.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When our investments enable individuals to remain embedded in shared institutions across life stages, they strengthen not only individual outcomes but our collective capacity to act in times of uncertainty and change.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In that sense, the effectiveness of this Budget lies not only in terms of the opportunities it creates but in the extent to which it enables Singaporeans to participate, contribute and remain connected over time.

sections.label: Surpluses enable strategic investment
sections.summary: Surpluses last year and this year give capacity to invest prudently and strategically in people.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: With surpluses last year and this year, we have the capacity to invest prudently and strategically in our people.

sections.label: Daily costs top concern
sections.summary: About 60% of over 1,000 respondents cited daily costs as their top concern and nearly one in five highlighted housing pressures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: About 60% of over 1,000 respondents cited daily costs as their top concern and nearly one in five highlighted housing pressures.

sections.label: Career progression employment challenge
sections.summary: Nearly half of 433 respondents cited lack of career progression as their biggest challenge and over one in four mentioned underemployment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: On employment, nearly half of 433 respondents cited lack of career progression as their biggest challenge and more than one in four mentioned underemployment.

sections.label: AI courses and training gaps
sections.summary: Over 100,000 Singaporeans took AI-related courses last year; one in five felt unprepared and nearly half lacked sufficient training.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Over 100,000 Singaporeans took AI-related courses last year – a positive sign.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: One in five survey respondents felt unprepared for AI-related shifts in their industry and nearly half said they lacked sufficient training due to time constraints or difficulty finding relevant programmes.

sections.label: Volunteer active mobility safety initiative
sections.summary: Vareck Ng co-founded a volunteer initiative to improve safety for walkers and cyclists, working with LTA's Active Mobility Team.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Vareck Ng, a young resident, co-founded a volunteer initiative to improve safety for active mobility users, both walkers and cyclists.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Together, we identified problem spots and worked with the Land Transport Authority's (LTA's) Active Mobility Team to improve safety.

sections.label: Stable jobs and affordable housing
sections.summary: When young people have stable jobs and affordable housing, they can plan with peace of mind and start families and careers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: When young people have stable jobs and affordable housing, they can plan their lives with peace of mind and start families and careers.

sections.label: Budget investment in people
sections.summary: The Budget's most important investment is in people across every generation, especially those who will carry Singapore forward.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: The most important investment in this Budget is not in technology alone.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: It is in our people across every generation, especially those who will carry Singapore forward.

sections.label: AI already reshaping industries
sections.summary: AI is already here and reshaping industries, changing how some tasks are done, and moving faster than most forecasts predicted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: AI is here, AI is not arriving, AI is not five years away, but it is already reshaping industries, changing how some tasks are being done and it is moving faster than most forecasts predicted even three years ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: What AI does best today and will get better at doing tomorrow is work that is repetitive, rule-based or data heavy.

sections.label: Humans controlling AI use
sections.summary: Singapore's job is to ensure humans remain in control of how AI is used and not let it dictate our values.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Singapore's job and this includes my job, is to make sure that we as humans remain in control of how AI is used and not let it dictate our values.

sections.label: Human accountability and AI governance
sections.summary: Human accountability requires robust and ethical AI governance frameworks, regulatory frameworks on disallowed AI content, and a clear chain of accountability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: What will also not change is the need for human accountability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: And accountability means developing AI governance frameworks that are robust and ethical.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Accountability also means recognising the risks and dangers of AI, developing regulatory frameworks on what AI content should be disallowed for certain audiences and making sure there is a clear chain of accountability.

sections.label: SkillsFuture credits used by Singaporeans
sections.summary: More than half a million Singaporeans used their SkillsFuture credits last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: More than half a million Singaporeans used their SkillsFuture credits last year.

sections.label: Lower risk ways for SMEs
sections.summary: SMEs do not want to be first movers, so lower risk, structured ways will be created for them to experiment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: They tell me: "Jasmin, you want us to be early adopters, but we do not want to be the first movers." They have personal experiences of trying out new technologies and then realising that the technologies became outdated too fast.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: We will create lower risk, structured ways for our SMEs to experiment.

sections.label: AI funding shifts to implementation
sections.summary: Funding support shifts from set-up costs to implementation, business process redesign, reskilling and changing how organisations operate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: When IT adoption was the main challenge, the barrier was set-up cost, so we subsidised set-up costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Today, an early-stage AI prototype can be built in just a few hours.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: So, the barrier now is capability and workflow redesign.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Our funding support will shift accordingly towards implementation, business process redesign, reskilling and the much harder work of changing how an organisation actually operates.

sections.label: Education focus on judgement and values
sections.summary: AI will force education to focus on judgement, values and working with AI rather than competing with it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: AI will force us to sharpen the focus of education on what truly matters – judgement, values and the ability to work with AI rather than compete with it.

sections.label: Helping children sharpen judgement skills
sections.summary: Work will be done on areas like sharpening judgement in uncertain situations so children remain master of AI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: How do we help them sharpen their judgement skills, especially in uncertain situations?

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: These are all areas that we will be working on, so that our children grow up confident that they remain the master of AI – and not the other way around.

sections.label: Staying in control of AI
sections.summary: People must always control AI and intentionally decide what it is used for, building a wiser society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Most importantly, we must always be in control of AI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: We must intentionally decide what AI should be used for, even if it nudges us to think otherwise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: This is how we can build not just a smarter economy, but a wiser and a more confident society, ready for the journey ahead.

sections.label: Parents pressured supporting children and parents
sections.summary: A 2019 NTUC Income study reported 94% of parents surveyed felt pressured supporting growing children and ageing parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: As far back as 2019, NTUC Income research reported that 94% of parents surveyed revealed that they were currently pressured between having to financially support their growing children and their ageing parents.

sections.label: Family schemes from third child onwards
sections.summary: Government support like $500 Child LifeSG Credits is welcomed, but many family schemes benefit only from the third child.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The Government has provided broad-based support and I welcome measures, such as the additional $500 in Child LifeSG Credits in this year's Budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: However, many of our structural family schemes are still designed to provide additional benefits only from the third child onwards.

sections.label: Singapore carbon tax rate
sections.summary: Singapore has Asia's highest carbon tax, and the rate will likely settle at the lower end of the $50 to $80 per tonne band by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: On carbon pricing, Singapore already has the highest carbon tax in Asia.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: So, I welcome the Prime Minister's pragmatic stance that the rate will likely settle at the lower end of the $50 to $80 per tonne band by 2030.

sections.label: Solar energy targets
sections.summary: Singapore met its two gigawatts peak solar target ahead of time, and revised targets of three gigawatts peak by 2030 are welcome.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: On solar energy, we achieved our two gigawatts peak target ahead of time – an impressive feat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The revised targets to three gigawatts peak by 2030 are welcome.

sections.label: Diversifying Singapore energy mix
sections.summary: Diversifying the energy mix through natural gas, solar, regional power imports, low-carbon solutions and potentially nuclear energy requires partnership, regulations, funding and a technology ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Diversifying our energy mix – through natural gas, solar, regional power imports, low-carbon solutions and potentially nuclear energy – is paramount to the survival and resilience of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: It requires a deeper and more deliberate partnership between Government and industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: We must establish enabling regulations, dedicated funding mechanisms and a robust ecosystem of technology providers, project developers and reliable baseload off takers.

sections.label: Property owners and SMEs
sections.summary: Private property owners face a 15-month wait-out period before buying resale HDB flats, and SMEs employing 70% of the workforce struggle amid AI adoption and digital transformation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: There are private property owners subject to a 15-month wait-out period before purchasing resale HDB flats even when they may have legitimate reasons for needing to right-size quickly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: There are the SMEs that employ 70% of our workforce yet struggle even as we push ahead with AI adoption and digital transformation.

sections.label: SME AI adoption rates
sections.summary: Budget 2026 places AI at the centre of strategy; in 2024 only 14.5% of SMEs adopted AI, up from 4.2%, while larger firms rose from 44% to 62.5%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The question is whether we will shape this transformation deliberately – upgrading our firms, our companies, our businesses and uplifting our workers – or risk allowing intelligent systems to outpace our preparedness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: They make up 99% of our enterprises and employ 70% of our workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Budget 2026 places AI at the centre of our strategy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In 2024, only 14.5% of SMEs adopted AI – up from 4.2% the year before.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Now, that is progress, but still fewer than one in six.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, adoption amongst the larger firms surged from 44% to 62.5%.

sections.label: Budget 2026 wage support
sections.summary: Budget 2026 strengthens wage support by raising the Local Qualifying Salary, enhancing the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme and continuing the Progressive Wage approach.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Budget 2026 already strengthens wage support, raising the Local Qualifying Salary, enhancing the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme and continuing the Progressive Wage approach.

sections.label: National early warning mobility system
sections.summary: Move number one proposes a national early warning and mobility system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Move number one, a national early warning and mobility system.

sections.label: Mandatory workforce plans for AI
sections.summary: Move number two makes workforce plans mandatory for major AI support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Move number two, make workforce plans mandatory for major AI support.

sections.label: Global Ready Talent internships
sections.summary: Programmes like Enterprise Singapore's Global Ready Talent scheme show structured internships can build capability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Programmes such as Enterprise Singapore’s Global Ready Talent scheme show how structured internships can build capability.

sections.label: Job pathways for seniors, disabled
sections.summary: Move four builds concrete job pathways for seniors and persons with disabilities using physical AI and expanded supported employment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Move four, on building concrete job pathways for seniors and persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For seniors, physical AI can reduce strain and extend employability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Robotic lifting aids in logistics, autonomous carts in healthcare, AI-assisted scheduling to reduce cognitive load.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For persons with disabilities, we should expand supported employment into AI-adjacent roles: AI system monitoring and quality assurance, data labelling and validation with assistive tools, accessibility testing of AI systems, digital customer service roles using adaptive interfaces.

sections.label: AI for good fund, SSA backbone
sections.summary: Budget 2026 should create an AI for good fund and an SSA AI Backbone, with AI adoption deep, worker-centred and inclusive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Budget 2026 should create an “AI for good fund” to build an “SSA AI Backbone” comprising centralised AI tools for SSAs, shared data governance frameworks, volunteer AI professionals embedded in agencies, a vetted AI solutions marketplace.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: When SSAs become AI-enabled, the most vulnerable of us benefit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Ambition is necessary, but it is execution that determines whether progress is shared.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: AI adoption must be deep not cosmetic, worker-centred, inclusive by design, accessible to SMEs and supportive of the vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: If we get this right, Singapore will not merely adopt AI.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: We will prove that a nation can move fast in this space and still move together.

sections.label: Singapore chips, green, AI governance
sections.summary: Singapore produces 10% of chips and 20% of semiconductor equipment, leads in green transition, and is a global reference point in AI governance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Singapore today produces 10% of chips globally and 20% of semiconductor equipment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: We are a regional leader in enabling green transition, with Southeast Asia’s first carbon tax and a national hydrogen strategy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In AI governance and digital trust, frameworks, like the AI Verify and our Digital Economy Agreements, place us as a global reference point.

sections.label: Budget 2026 care subsidies
sections.summary: Budget 2026 provides higher preschool subsidies, expanded student care support and enhanced long-term care subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Budget 2026 takes meaningful steps in providing for higher preschool subsidies, expanded student care support and enhanced long-term care subsidies.

sections.label: Ageing Singaporeans by 2030
sections.summary: By 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be aged 65 or above.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Because by 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be aged 65 or above.

sections.label: Simplifying access and partnerships
sections.summary: The next task is making measures simple to access, aligned with employer needs and meaningful on the ground, with continued focus on simplifying access, partnerships and community support ecosystems.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Our next task is to make these measures simple to access, aligned with employer needs and meaningful for Singaporeans on the ground.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I support Budget 2026 for the clarity of the strategies to take Singapore forward.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I call for continued focus on simplifying access, strengthening partnerships and building community level support ecosystems.

sections.label: Business support in Budget
sections.summary: The Budget proposes corporate income tax rebate, enhanced Enterprise Financing Schemes and higher overseas expansion support, but businesses must have confidence to take the first step.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Budget proposes corporate income tax rebate, enhancements to Enterprise Financing Schemes and higher support levels for overseas expansion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: But the important thing is that businesses must have the confidence to take the first step.

sections.label: Raising productivity not costs
sections.summary: The goal of the policy is to raise productivity and not to inflate business cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The goal of our policy is to raise productivity and not to inflate business cost.

sections.label: Transparency, tiered support, capacity building
sections.summary: It calls for transparency on cost and effect, tiered support so SMEs avoid excessive cost burdens, and subsidies to encourage capacity building, not just buying systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, let businesses understand clearly the cost and effect, increasing transparency; Second, tiered support to prevent SMEs from bearing excessive cost burdens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Third, subsidies are to encourage capacity building, not just to buy systems.

sections.label: Fiscal surplus and long-term spending
sections.summary: A fiscal surplus provides a buffer, but population ageing, healthcare, climate adaptation and technology require long-term spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: A fiscal surplus provides a buffer for the nation, but fiscal planning has never been merely about annual balance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Population ageing, rising healthcare expenditure, climate adaptation investments and technological transformation require long-term spending.

sections.label: SMEs, AI and university partnerships
sections.summary: An SME was quoted a six-figure AI sum, but students proposed solutions covering about 70% of its needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: They acknowledged that AI is the way forward and recognise the need to embrace it in order to remain competitive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, one SME shared with me that when he approached an AI vendor to explore solutions for his business, he was quoted a six-figure sum, a significant investment that many smaller enterprises would understandably find daunting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: To his surprise, the students were able to propose multiple variable solutions that address about 70% of his business needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Beyond providing grants for SMEs to engage IT vendors, can we also foster stronger partnership between SMEs and our universities and polytechnics?

sections.label: Fiscal surplus size
sections.summary: The fiscal surplus is the all-time-largest in absolute terms at $15 billion, or 1.9% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The elephant in the room, which many Members have spoken about, is our fiscal surplus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is the all-time-largest in absolute terms, at $15 billion for the past financial year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Even by this measure, at 1.9%, it is substantial.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Around 10 years ago in 2017, our surplus was at 2.3% of GDP.

sections.label: Corporate income tax collections
sections.summary: Corporate income tax collections have been far higher after COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Zooming out, the multi-year picture is that corporate income tax collections have been far higher after COVID-19.

sections.label: Fiscal planning uncertainty next year
sections.summary: Fiscal planning will enter a period of higher uncertainty next year as the domestic top-up tax and BEPS measures kick in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: A short-termist and insecure Government would have taken a more popular approach to redirect security spending to more direct social benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: That said, fiscal planning will enter a period of higher uncertainty next year as the impact of the domestic top-up tax and other Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS)-related measures kick in.

sections.label: Population decline without immigration
sections.summary: At current fertility and without immigration, the number of Singaporeans will more than halve in each generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: At current levels of fertility and without immigration, the number of Singaporeans will more than halve in each generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: By SG100, without immigration, our citizen population could even revert to the same size as when we first became independent.

sections.label: Elderly poverty and Silver Support
sections.summary: The speaker advocates eradicating elderly poverty and increasing Silver Support payouts, with the highest tier for seniors above 80 or 85 in HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Elderly poverty should be eradicated, especially for the generations that grew up in a less developed Singapore and without the lifelong support of retirement policies that are in place today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I continue to advocate for Silver Support payouts to be increased and for the highest tier of Silver Support to be given to seniors above the age of 80 or 85 who live in HDB flats.

sections.label: Fiscal surplus CDC vouchers
sections.summary: The speaker proposes that fiscal surpluses above 2% of GDP be returned to all Singaporeans the following year through extra CDC vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For example, any fiscal surpluses above 2% of GDP should be given back to all Singaporeans in the following year through extra CDC vouchers.

sections.label: Salary support for jobseekers
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the Government give employers time-limited salary support to hire jobseekers actively looking for work at least six months, regardless of age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For example, the Government could give all employers time-limited salary support to hire any jobseeker who has been actively looking for a job for at least six months, regardless of age.

sections.label: No major revenue raising to 2035
sections.summary: The speaker says the fiscal surplus should let the Government assure Singaporeans it would not take major revenue raising moves up to 2035, barring material adverse circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Fourth and finally, amidst continued cost of living anxieties, the fiscal surplus should give the Government more confidence to assure Singaporeans that it would not take major revenue raising moves up to 2035, barring any material adverse circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Thus far, it has only said that it would not raise GST until 2030.

sections.label: Tax policies for wealth inequality
sections.summary: The speaker says tax policies should reduce wealth inequality through a more progressive property tax system, higher taxes on investment properties and progressive stamp duties on inherited properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We should continue to use tax policies to achieve other objectives, such as reducing wealth inequality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This can be achieved by making our property tax system more progressive, by being more aggressive with taxes for investment properties and by imposing progressive stamp duties on properties at the point of inheritance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Ensuring that we do not tax more than we need to spend.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And if there are surprises in our fiscal projections, it is better to be surprised by a surplus and never by a deficit.

sections.label: Conservative fiscal projections and surplus sharing
sections.summary: The speaker says fiscal projections should stay conservative, with a systematic surplus sharing mechanism for unexpected surpluses, and notes a surplus $8.29 billion above estimate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
sentences.text: My takeaway from his speech was that Mr Giam was suggesting that we run less conservative fiscal projections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
sentences.text: My suggestion and my view is that we should still be conservative with our fiscal projections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
sentences.text: And twined with my idea that if we run unexpected budget surpluses, we should have that as a systematic surplus sharing mechanism in the next year with all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: Actually, I think we are on the same page.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: I do believe that we should run a small surplus whenever possible, but that is different from running a surplus that is $8.29 billion more than what was estimated.

sections.label: Budget surplus under 2%
sections.summary: The last financial year did not have a budget surplus of more than 2%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
sentences.text: In fact, in the last financial year we did not run a budget surplus of more than 2%.

sections.label: PMET share of employed residents
sections.summary: MOM's Labour Force in Singapore 2025 report states 64% of employed residents are in PMET roles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: According to MOM's report on the Labour Force in Singapore 2025, 64% of our employed residents are in PMET roles.

sections.label: Workforce exposure to AI
sections.summary: Singapore's workforce is highly exposed to AI because of the large share of such roles in the economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Singapore’s workforce is highly exposed to AI due to the large share of such roles in our economy.

sections.label: TechSkills Accelerator expansion to professions
sections.summary: Expanding the TechSkills Accelerator to accountancy and legal professions offers opportunities by strengthening capability-building in sectors facing talent and retention challenges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: In particular, the expansion of the TechSkills Accelerator to the accountancy and legal professions presents opportunities by strengthening capability-building in these sectors, which are facing ongoing talent and retention challenges.

sections.label: AI help for lawyers and accountants
sections.summary: The speaker hopes assistance helps lawyers and accountants work more efficiently and improve output, while noting mid-career lawyers and accountants are not AI-natives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I hope that we direct the assistance to help lawyers and accountants to work more efficiently and improve their overall work output, so that they can focus on honing the core skills of the profession.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: That said, we must recognise and be cognisant of the fact that mid-career lawyers and accountants are not AI-natives.

sections.label: AI adoption and foreign companies
sections.summary: Supporting lawyers and accountants in adopting AI will strengthen Singapore's attractiveness to foreign companies hiring Singaporeans or setting up headquarters here.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Supporting them in their adoption of AI will also strengthen Singapore's attractiveness to foreign companies looking to hire Singaporeans or to set up headquarters in Singapore.

sections.label: Champions of AI programme support
sections.summary: The Champions of AI programme tailors support to each company, including enterprise transformation and workforce training, and the speaker hopes Government will consider it alongside established schemes for micro- and small SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The newly announced Champions of AI programme will go some way to support this by tailoring support to each company, including enterprise transformation and workforce training.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government will consider the Champions of AI programme alongside the more established schemes, such as the Enterprise Innovation Scheme and the Productivity Solutions Grant to marry the two for micro- and small SMEs, who often face their own unique sets of constraints on cashflows, cost, implementation expertise and change management.

sections.label: Uneven take-up of family workplace support
sections.summary: Take-up of family related workplace support remains uneven, and MOM and NTUC work with partners on tripartite guidelines and programmes for flexible work arrangements and return-to-work pathways.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Despite stronger policies, take-up of family related workplace support across employers and employees remain uneven, reflecting the continued influence of workplace expectations and culture on employees' confidence to take time for family responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: MOM and NTUC have been working with their partners on this front to set clearer norms for flexible work arrangements, to help enterprises understand how to structure return-to-work pathways and job design that accommodates caregiving responsibilities, through tripartite guidelines and programmes with industry partners.

sections.label: Workplace response and HR practices
sections.summary: The difference lies in how workplaces interpret and respond to these moments and how managers communicate, and the speaker hopes Government works with industry partners to shape HR practices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The difference lies in how workplaces interpret and respond to these moments, and how managers are equipped to communicate with care, make balanced decisions and plan for continuity without placing undue strain on teams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government can work with the industry partners, such as the tripartite Institute for Human Resource Professionals, to shape HR practices and standards across industries to place greater emphasis on consistent and fair implementation of family-friendly workplace practices.

sections.label: Aligned education, workplaces and support structures
sections.summary: A system aligned across education, workplaces and support structures gives individuals space to decide with confidence and contribute over time, strengthening opportunity and resilience in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: A system that is aligned across education, workplaces and support structures, gives individuals the space to make decisions with confidence and to contribute meaningfully over time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: This is how we can strengthen both opportunity and resilience in Singapore.

sections.label: WEF AI job displacement estimate
sections.summary: The World Economic Forum estimates that by 2030 AI and related technologies could displace 92 million jobs while creating 170 million new roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The World Economic Forum estimates that by 2030, AI and related technologies could displace 92 million jobs, while creating 170 million new roles, reflecting a profound structural shift in how work is done.

sections.label: AWS research on AI skills gap
sections.summary: AWS-commissioned research found nearly 94% of employers expect employees to be AI-driven by 2028, yet 74% report difficulty finding AI talent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Research commissioned by Amazon Web Services (AWS) on AI adoption and skills in Singapore found that nearly 94% of employers expect their employees to be AI-driven by 2028, yet, 74% report difficulty finding the AI talent they need, highlighting a clear skills gap between demand and supply.

sections.label: Gen Z AI skills demand
sections.summary: AWS research showed 91% of Generation Z in Singapore want to acquire AI skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The same AWS research also showed that 91% of Generation Z in Singapore want to acquire AI skills, underscoring both the urgency and willingness of our youths to embrace this transformation.

sections.label: Personal Learning Devices for secondary students
sections.summary: Singapore provided Personal Learning Devices to all secondary students from 2020, fully implemented by end of 2021, with financial assistance schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Singapore has already taken a decisive step by providing Personal Learning Devices (PLDs) to all secondary students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Introduced progressively from 2020 and fully implemented by the end of 2021, these devices were integrated with the national e-learning platform, the Student Learning Space and was supported by financial assistance schemes to ensure that no student – no secondary school student – was left behind.

sections.label: EdTech Masterplan and Budget 2026
sections.summary: EdTech Masterplan 2030 makes digital literacy a national priority, and Budget 2026 highlights harnessing AI as a strategic advantage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As Singapore's EdTech Masterplan 2030 reflects, strengthening students' digital literacy and technological skills is a national priority to, "prepare students for a technology transformed world".

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, access to appropriate hardware ensures that all students – all students – regardless of background, can engage effectively with emerging digital tools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This aligns with Budget 2026, which highlights harnessing AI as a strategic advantage to build a resilient and skilled workforce.

sections.label: Extending PLDs to primary schools
sections.summary: The speaker renews a call for the Government to extend Personal Learning Devices to primary school students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In this way, equitable access to PLDs in primary schools is not merely an educational measure, but a strategic investment in Singapore's long-term human capital and technological competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On this note, I would like to renew my call to the Government to make that decision to extend PLDs to primary school students.

sections.label: Expanding Graduate Industry Traineeships Programme
sections.summary: The speaker says traineeships should be expanded to AI strategy focus sectors and people-centric industries like social services and retail.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Government introduced the Graduate Industry Traineeships Programme last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In addition to financial services and information and communications, traineeships should be expanded to include the newly announced focus sectors in Singapore's AI strategy – advanced manufacturing, connectivity and even healthcare – as well as people-centric industries, such as social services sectors and retail.

sections.label: S Pass salary benchmarks for construction
sections.summary: With higher S Pass minimum qualifying salaries, a sector-based skills-focused approach is suggested for construction, with benchmarks reflecting skills rather than age tiers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With the increase in minimum qualifying salaries for S Pass holders, a more sector-based and skills-focused approach may be needed for construction, where structural manpower shortages persist and margins are unhealthily eroded.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Salary benchmarks should better reflect skills, experience and job responsibilities, rather than relying heavily on age tiers alone.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and flexi-work arrangements
sections.summary: The passage proposes doubling down on SkillsFuture for parents and making flexi-work a mainstream feature of good jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One starting point is to double down on SkillsFuture for these parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Flexi-work arrangements should become a mainstream feature of good jobs – not an exception, but an integral part of how we attract, retain and empower workers across every life stage.

sections.label: Seniors employment in super-aged Singapore
sections.summary: The passage states that to assist seniors in employment, Singapore is set to become a super-aged society this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Fourth, to assist our seniors in employment, Singapore is set to become a super-aged society this year.

sections.label: Mature workers pilot and matching service
sections.summary: The passage notes the AfA-EMW pilot programme and suggests a matching service connecting industry veterans with SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Last year, the Alliance for Action on Empowering Multi-Stage Careers for Mature Workers (AfA-EMW) launched a pilot programme, collaborating with various parties to jointly create solutions for re-skilling, alternative employment models and progressive retirement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While this is a positive start, we should also care for those seniors who prefer a low commitment but high impact work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I suggest establishing a matching service, such as connecting industry veterans with SMEs to serve as consultants, subject matter experts or trainers.

sections.label: Silver Support payment reductions
sections.summary: The passage states appeals were received from residents whose Silver Support payments were reduced or ceased due to per capita household income changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The scheme is well-intentioned and has benefited many seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: However, I have received appeals from residents whose Silver Support payments were reduced or ceased due to changes in per capita household income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: First, when adult children begin working, even in modest-paying jobs, their parents' Silver Support may be reduced despite no improvement in the seniors' own retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Second, when elderly parents move in with their children, the household per capita income (HPCI) rises, potentially reducing eligibility.

sections.label: Wage support percentages
sections.summary: The passage states wage support can reach up to 70%, and up to 90% for eligible workers aged 40 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Today, wage support can reach up to 70%, and up to 90% for eligible workers aged 40 and above.

sections.label: SME Centres and AI adoption
sections.summary: The passage asks the Prime Minister what expanded role SME Centres will play in accelerating AI adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: SME Centres play a pivotal role in building awareness and guiding adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, may I ask the Prime Minister what expanded role SME Centres will play in accelerating AI adoption?

sections.label: Preventive Health Data Sandbox proposal
sections.summary: The passage proposes a Preventive Health Data Sandbox and a national certification framework for preventive AI algorithms, noting Singapore's existing investments and Familial Hypercholesterolaemia screening.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Building on these strengths, we could consider establishing a dedicated Preventive Health Data Sandbox, a secure environment where approved enterprises and research institutions validate AI-driven diagnostic and risk prediction models using structured national datasets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In tandem, a national certification framework for preventive AI algorithms could strengthen international credibility, enabling solutions validated here to be deployed across the region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Singapore is already taking important steps through research, innovation and enterprise investments and initiatives such as subsidised Familial Hypercholesterolaemia genetic screening with MediSave support.

sections.label: Singapore blended capital mobilisation
sections.summary: Singapore is well-positioned to mobilise blended capital as foundations, philanthropies and family offices increasingly prioritise wellness, longevity and population health investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Singapore is well-positioned to mobilise blended capital, as foundations, philanthropies and family offices increasingly prioritise investments in wellness, longevity and population health.

sections.label: Preventive healthcare investment and Budget surplus
sections.summary: Investing in AI-powered preventive and precision healthcare with blended capital can improve lives and create jobs; a $15.1 billion Budget surplus is likely the largest since 1965.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: By investing in preventive and precision healthcare powered by AI and strengthened through blended capital, we can build an economy that improves lives while creating new job opportunities for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, a Budget surplus of $15.1 billion is likely the largest in absolute terms since 1965.

sections.label: Setting aside surplus as strategic reserves
sections.summary: Given geopolitical tensions and economic volatility, the speaker supports setting aside about half the surplus as strategic reserves for possible economic crisis in the next few years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Given the global geopolitical tensions and economic volatility, I support setting aside about half of the surplus as strategic reserves, in the event that there might be economic crisis in the next few three or four years, so that it can be used to stimulate the economy and support Singaporeans.

sections.label: GST increase annual yield
sections.summary: The two-percentage points GST increase will yield an estimated $3 billion to $4 billion annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The two-percentage points GST increase will yield an estimated $3 billion to $4 billion annually.

sections.label: Extra CDC vouchers suggestion
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the Government distribute an extra $200 in CDC vouchers to Singaporeans over 21 years old, noting the same amount does not mean equality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Hence, the same amount does not mean equality here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I will like to suggest that the Government distribute an extra $200 CDC vouchers to Singaporeans over 21 years old.

sections.label: HDB blocks without lift access
sections.summary: About 100 HDB blocks still lack direct lift access to every floor because of high costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Currently, approximately 100 HDB blocks still do not have direct lift access to every floor due to high costs.

sections.label: Support for adults with special needs
sections.summary: Support for adults with special needs remains limited, with insufficient vocational training, retraining and workforce reintegration opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Currently, support for adults with special needs remains limited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Opportunities for continuous vocational training, skills retraining, or reintegrating into the workforce after experiencing setbacks are still insufficient.

sections.label: Special needs foundation proposal
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to consider dedicated resources for a special needs foundation funding long-term projects, research and community support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: For these families, the issue is no longer about opportunities, but about dignity, stability and peace of mind for the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Therefore, I hereby call upon the Government to consider allocating dedicated resources to establish a special needs foundation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: This foundation could fund long-term projects, research and community support to, where possible, help adults with special needs, maintain employability and stay connected with society and provide empathetic and structured care for those with special needs who cannot work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Let us walk along persons with special needs, not only during their childhood but throughout their entire lives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: It represents the collective sacrifices made by workers, businesses and families during difficult times through paying taxes, adapting to GST increases and tightening their belts.

sections.label: NTUC survey on economic sentiments
sections.summary: NTUC's 2025 survey of 2,000 workers found cost of living, job security and AI-related job displacement among their concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: As the Secretary-General of the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC), I am keenly aware that for many of our workers and families, these disruptive forces are not distant issues but daily lived experiences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: This is reflected in NTUC's Survey on Economic Sentiments, which was conducted in 2025 polling 2,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Cost of living remains a key concern – 37%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Job security was the top concern for nearly 20% of them too, due to factors, such as economic uncertainties and technological changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Close to 20% were anxious about artificial intelligence (AI)-related job displacement or had already experienced some negative impact due to AI.

sections.label: AI-Ready SG subscription support
sections.summary: Through AI-Ready SG, union members get NTUC funding support offsetting up to 50% of unfunded subscription costs for eligible AI tools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Concretely, through AI-Ready SG, union members will get NTUC funding support to offset up to 50% of unfunded subscription costs for eligible AI tools.

sections.label: Employer headcount freezes, PME anxiety
sections.summary: A SNEF survey found 60% of polled employers planned headcount freezes, while an NTUC survey found almost 40% of PMEs anxious about keeping jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Among the employers polled in a survey by the Singapore National Employers' Federation (SNEF), nearly three in five, or 60%, planned to freeze headcount this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: NTUC's own survey found that almost 40% of PMEs were anxious about whether they could still keep their jobs beyond the next six months.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support income cap
sections.summary: Only workers earning $5,000 or less monthly qualify for the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme, and exceeding this cap caused 60% of September 2025 rejections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Today, only workers earning $5,000 or less monthly are eligible for the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme (JSS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: As of September 2025, exceeding this income cap was one of the reasons for 60% of applications to be rejected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: One possible approach is to peg the income threshold to the professional, manager, executive and technician (PMET) median monthly income, which was around $7,600 in 2025.

sections.label: NTUC support for workers and PMEs
sections.summary: NTUC will work with Government and employers to help workers be AI-ready, support vulnerable workers and PMEs, and backs this Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: NTUC will continue to work with the Government and employers to ensure that every worker can stand on firm footing during the transitions, with peace of mind at work and at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Let us empower every worker be AI-ready, strengthen support to those vulnerable to disruption and strengthen the Labour Movement's ability to protect and uplift our PMEs in this age where it is no longer just the blue-collar workers that may face technological disruption, but with AI disrupting the white-collar space as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement will continue advocating for measures that support workers today and improve their prospects for tomorrow, whether it is helping young graduates into good first jobs, supporting PMEs to navigate career transitions or ensuring caregivers can stay employed while caring for their families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the points I have raised on behalf of the Labour Movement, I stand in support of this Budget.

sections.label: Skills, trade, ageing and fertility trends
sections.summary: The report projects 40% of skills will change by 2030, tariffs quadrupled, over 21% of residents are 65 or above, and TFR is below half replacement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The World Economic Forum's Future of Jobs Report projects that nearly 40% of skills being used in today's workforce will change by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Global trade tensions continue to intensify, with the value of goods hit by new tariffs quadrupling in the past year to the highest level in over 15 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As of this year, we are now an officially super-aged society, with more than 21% of our resident population 65 or above.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: At the same time, our resident total fertility rate (TFR) stands at less than half the replacement rate.

sections.label: Citizens aged 80 and older
sections.summary: The number of citizens aged 80 and older increased by about 60% over the past decade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The number of citizens aged 80 and older have increased by approximately 60% over the past decade.

sections.label: Malay total fertility rate
sections.summary: The Malay TFR is below the population replacement rate, at 1.58 in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   Sir, family is the bedrock of our society's strength.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, the reality we must face is that the TFR of Malays is now below the population replacement rate, at 1.58 in 2024.

sections.label: Seniors needing daily living assistance
sections.summary: By 2030, around 100,000 seniors are expected to require assistance with daily living.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: (In English): By 2030, around 100,000 seniors are expected to require assistance with daily living.

sections.label: Caregiver support and HCG criteria
sections.summary: Speaker seeks stronger caregiver support frameworks and broader HCG qualifying criteria to include those unable to work due to mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Today, many rely on annual leave and career often competes with caregiving responsibilities until a point where one feels like they have to tap out of the workforce, especially for women who tend to disproportionately carry the caregiving load; having stronger caregiver support frameworks, including hospital post-discharge protocols, as well as helping caregivers begin again after their loved ones are no longer around.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope we broaden the qualifying criteria of the HCG to include those who are unable to work due to mental health conditions, instead of only assessing by activities of daily living.

sections.label: Ageing population in Singapore
sections.summary: By 2050 nearly half of Singaporeans are projected to be over 65, and 40% of Ang Mo Kio residents are over 60.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: By 2050, nearly half of Singaporeans are projected to be over 65.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In Ang Mo Kio, 40% of our residents are over 60 years old.

sections.label: Intergenerational compact and belonging
sections.summary: Intentional design and a stronger compact between generations should ensure longevity does not feel lonely or weaken Singapore, with every generation having a place.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: If we design intentionally and strengthen the compact between generations, then longevity will not feel lonely and will not weaken Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And whether one comes home to a large reunion, bringing the next generation along, or a small gathering, or a community who becomes family – every generation of Singaporeans should know, that they always have a place at our national table.

sections.label: Projected budget surplus
sections.summary: The projected surplus of $15 billion is more than double the earlier estimate of $7 billion, a stark reminder of a recurring pattern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The projected surplus of $15 billion, more than double the earlier estimate of $7 billion, is a stark reminder of a recurring pattern.

sections.label: GST hike and revenue projections
sections.summary: Speaker questions the urgency of the GST hike given higher-than-projected resources, noting GST revenue rose from an estimated $12.8 billion in Budget 2022 to $22.3 billion this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It begs the question of whether the urgency behind tax increases, such as the Goods and Services Tax (GST) hike, was truly justified when the state consistently finds itself with more resources than initially projected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And also, based on my checks, when announced in 2022, the GST hike was projected to bring about $3.5 billion annually when the full hike is in place by 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: GST revenue was initially estimated at $12.8 billion in Budget 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This year, GST revenue is estimated at $22.3 billion, an almost $10 billion increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The most notable of which is the exclusion of land sale proceeds, amounting to $21 billion in 2025 and estimated at $21 billion in 2026.

sections.label: MOF paper on wealth inequality
sections.summary: The MOF Occasional Paper published on 9 February provided the first-ever public release of Singapore's wealth data, showing wealth inequality with a Gini coefficient of 0.55 exceeds income inequality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I was initially hopeful, when the recently released the Ministry of Finance's (MOF's) Occasional Paper on "Income Growth, Inequality and Social Mobility Trends in Singapore" was published on 9 February, ahead of Prime Minister Wong's Budget Statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This paper provided the first-ever public release of Singapore's wealth data, which revealed that Singapore's wealth inequality, with a Gini coefficient of 0.55, exceeds that of income inequality.

sections.label: Bringing back estate duty
sections.summary: The passage states estate duty, abolished in 2008, must be seriously considered for bringing back.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Furthermore, we must seriously consider bringing back estate duty, which was abolished in 2008.

sections.label: PARF rebate cuts for cars
sections.summary: The passage states PARF rebates for a BMW 5-series and a Suzuki Swift will be slashed, raising the Swift's annual depreciation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A BMW 5-series, listed for around $370,000 will see its PARF rebate slashed from around $40,000 to $4,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But even an entry level Suzuki Swift, which is one of the cheapest cars in Singapore at a so-called mere $152,000, we will see its PARF rebate slash from $6,600 to $660, resulting in an increase to its annual depreciation to about $15,000.

sections.label: Falling total fertility rate
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore's TFR fell below 1.0 in 2023 and stayed there in 2024, threatening long-term sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Our TFR fell below 1.0 in 2023 and remained there in 2024, a trajectory that poses a profound threat to our long-term sustainability.

sections.label: Hungary's tax exemption for mothers
sections.summary: The passage states Hungary fully exempts mothers with three children from personal income tax, and now some mothers under 30.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The point here is this, that Hungary is fully exempting mothers with three children from paying personal income tax regardless of age and starting this year, even mothers under 30 with at least one child will be fully exempt.

sections.label: Budget childcare subsidies and credits
sections.summary: The passage states the childcare subsidy income ceiling rose from $12,000 to $15,000 and families get $500 in LifeSG Credits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As part of this year's Budget package, the household income ceiling for childcare subsidies was increased from $12,000 to $15,000, while families with children below 12 years old will receive $500 in LifeSG Credits.

sections.label: Reverting Working Mother's Child Relief
sections.summary: The passage states the speaker hopes the Government reverts to the previous WMCR, applicable only to mothers with children born before 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even if the Government does not wish to take the Hungarian approach, the least we can do is not make mothers pay more taxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And I have shared on many occasions in this House, I hope the Government would revert back to the previous iteration of the Working Mother's Child Relief (WMCR), which is applicable only to mothers with children born before 2024.

sections.label: 2025 projected surplus
sections.summary: The projected surplus for 2025 is $15.1 billion, more than double the initial estimate of $6.8 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The projected surplus for 2025 stands at $15.1 billion, more than double the initial estimate of $6.8 billion.

sections.label: GST revenue increase
sections.summary: Estimated total GST revenue was $12.8 billion then, and is projected to rise to $22.3 billion this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The estimated total GST revenue then was $12.8 billion, whilst this year, this figure is projected to soar to $22.3 billion, an increase of nearly $10 billion.

sections.label: Structural solutions for families
sections.summary: Drawing from international experience, comprehensive and structural solutions must be formulated to give Singaporeans confidence and capability to start families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Drawing from international experience, we must formulate comprehensive and structural solutions that give Singaporeans the confidence and capability to start families.

sections.label: Equitable social contract
