sections.summary: The passage asks whether to collect less tax from the surplus or let the demographic foundation wither while wealth concentrates, and calls for a more equitable social contract.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Is it collecting a few percentage points less in taxes from our record-breaking surplus or allowing the nation's demographic foundation to wither whilst wealth concentrates in the hands of a select few, leaving middle-class Singaporeans to foot the bill?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Let us build a more equitable, resilient and sustainable social contract.

sections.label: Advanced Mandatory Retrenchment Notifications
sections.summary: Introducing advanced Mandatory Retrenchment Notifications to unions and the Government can provide more timely and early intervention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: First, introducing advanced Mandatory Retrenchment Notifications (MRNs) to unions and the Government can provide more timely and early intervention.

sections.label: Sharing disruption information, raising JSS threshold
sections.summary: The Government can share disruption information with NTUC and unions, and consider raising the JSS income threshold from $5,000 to $7,600 to better cover PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Third, the Government can consider sharing information with NTUC and unions on sectors and companies that might be disrupted due to economic restructuring, including expected scale of impact and timeline, past retrenchment incidence, and past retrenchment benefit levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I am heartened that after a decade of lobbying, involuntarily unemployed workers facing temporary financial strain can now benefit from transitional support for up to six months while they undergo training or look for better-fitting jobs through the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme (JSS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In fact, from April to August last year, MOM also shared that 60% of the 7,200 JSS applications received were rejected, of which one of the top three reasons for unsuccessful applications was exceeding the income threshold of $5,000 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The Government can consider raising the income threshold from $5,000 to $7,600 to better cover PMEs.

sections.label: Term contract workers and graduates
sections.summary: The Government can encourage employers to convert FTC workers to permanent roles after two contract renewals, as fewer graduates secured permanent full-time positions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The Government can encourage employers to emplace FTC workers into permanent roles after two cycles of contract renewals, and regard successive contracts renewed within two months of the previous contract as continuous service, instead of the current one-month window stipulated in the Tripartite Advisory on the Employment of Term Contract Employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: According to the most recent Graduate Employment Surveys from autonomous universities, private education institutions and polytechnics, fewer graduates secured permanent full-time positions within six months of graduation across the board, even as starting salaries continued to rise.

sections.label: GRIT Programme extension
sections.summary: The Government can consider an extended, higher-value GRIT iteration in high-growth sectors, with host organisations required to convert trainees into permanent full-time employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The Government launched the GRIT Programme last year to absorb recruitment and training risk for employers while helping fresh graduates gain industry experience and relevant skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The Government can consider launching an extended and higher-value iteration of GRIT in high-growth and high-demand sectors with opportunities ranging from one to two years and with monthly traineeship allowances on-par with starting salaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Host organisations must convert trainees into permanent full-time employees unless a valid reason and supporting evidence are submitted.

sections.label: Employment Act Part IV thresholds
sections.summary: Lower-income PMEs are not covered under Part IV of the Employment Act, so the Government is called on to raise income thresholds for non-workmen to at least $3,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Lower-income PMEs, sometimes disguised, for example, are not covered under Part IV of the Employment Act which provides for rest days, hours of work and overtime pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I therefore call on the Government to increase the Employment Act Part IV income thresholds, something that I raised in this House before, for non-workmen to at least $3,000, which will better reflect today's workforce demographics and help curb overworking norms.

sections.label: Foreign PMEs and qualifying salaries
sections.summary: Policy should encourage foreign PMEs to complement the local workforce, and the Government's decision to raise qualifying salaries for EP and S Pass holders is welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The key is to create policy that encourages foreign PMEs to complement rather than displace the local workforce, encourage skill transfer and local-foreign integration and position local PMEs for senior and leadership positions as well as high-paying and high-value jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I therefore welcome the Government's decision to raise the qualifying salaries for and S Pass holders to maintain the quality of EP and S Pass holders as wages rise.

sections.label: Merging WSG and SSG
sections.summary: The Government is going to create a one-stop-shop new agency by merging WSG and SSG for skills training, career guidance and job matching.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: During SkillsFuture's 10th anniversary last year, I suggested to consolidate efforts and streamline offerings across different arms of the CET ecosystem including NTUC's e2i, WSG, SSG, training providers and the various Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs), to control quality and prevent overlap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Government considered the recommendation and are going to create now a one-stop-shop new agency for skills training, career guidance and job matching services by merging WSG and SSG.

sections.label: NTUC AI training pathways
sections.summary: NTUC will roll out AI training pathways and subsidise up to 50% of subscription costs of eligible AI tools for members for two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: NTUC will roll out AI training pathways and subsidise up to 50% of subscription costs of eligible AI tools for members, for an initial period of two years.

sections.label: Inclusive hiring and UEC scheme
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government embeds inclusive hiring in workforce policy and asks that the ended UEC scheme be extended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government continues to embed inclusive hiring into mainstream workforce policy to unlock under-utilised potential and ensure all workers can contribute fully and justly, as well as to boost the employment and employability of ex-offenders and persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I note that the UEC scheme ended on December 2025, and I ask that an extension be considered.

sections.label: Budget for the 5 U's
sections.summary: The speaker says persons with disabilities and ex-offenders are concentrated in lower-wage jobs and that this Budget must work for the "5 U's".

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: As persons with disabilities and ex-offenders are more likely to be concentrated in lower wage and lower-skilled jobs and sectors that have higher rates of unemployment and/or underemployment, a more concerted effort can also be made to prevent reproducing inequalities for these two groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: This is why this Budget must work for the "5 U's": the unemployed, the underemployed, the under-represented, the untrained and the underserved.

sections.label: Tripartite talks on Employment Act
sections.summary: The speaker notes SNEF's reservations, asks if SNEF agreed, and cites a Tripartite Workgroup reviewing the Employment Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The intention to pursue this point was made by NTUC before the Budget debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Shortly thereafter, the chief executive officer (CEO) of SNEF wrote to The Straits Times to share that, I think the words were: "they have strong reservations about this call." Can I ask the Member, in view of the tripartite framework, has there been agreement with SNEF on this particular point?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: On the Member's question, there are tripartite negotiations on this point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: We have formed a Tripartite Workgroup on the review of the Employment Act which I am a member, we are looking at this carefully to balance the interests of the respective tripartite partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: But what I shared earlier is our NTUC's standpoint, which both Secretary-General and myself have shared earlier.

sections.label: HDB blocks and Budget surplus
sections.summary: The speaker notes more HDB blocks are crossing 50 years and that the 2025 Budget surplus of over $15 billion goes to reserves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: But more and more of our HDB blocks are also crossing the 50-year mark.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is good news indeed that we had managed to achieve a Budget surplus of over $15 billion for 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The surplus will be added to our reserves, where we can generate investment income streams that will contribute to our future Budgets.

sections.label: HIP review and SERS request
sections.summary: The speaker asks HDB to review HIP policy for another flexible round, or otherwise seeks SERS for residents such as Henderson Crescent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: To deal with the systemic deterioration of such HDB blocks, could the HDB review its HIP policy and consider an additional round of HIP which is more flexible in scope to take into account the specific issues faced by a particular HDB estate?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: If that cannot be done, I would like to call upon the Government, on behalf of my residents, such as our residents from Henderson Crescent, to grant their request for Selective En bloc Redevelopment Scheme (SERS).

sections.label: Measures for sky garden disamenities
sections.summary: The speaker says disamenities persist despite efforts and appeals to MND to reconsider gantries, CCTVs, visitor limits and a fee.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: These problems have not abated, even with the concerted efforts of our grassroots volunteers, the HDB, Town Council, the National Environment Agency (NEA) and the police, disamenities still persist.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Hence, I appeal to MND once again, to reconsider my previous suggestions: install gantries for registration, install more closed circuit televisions (CCTVs) to monitor visitors and their activities, limit the number of visitors and require payment of a small fee to support the operations and cleaning of the sky gardens.

sections.label: Property tax rebate for seniors
sections.summary: A speaker asks the Government to consider a longer-term rebate for seniors no longer earning income but facing higher property taxes paid from savings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The anxiety is real, especially as they are no longer earning an income and yet face increasingly higher property taxes that they are paying for out of their own savings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government can consider granting a longer-term rebate for such cases.

sections.label: Low take-up of initiatives
sections.summary: The speaker worries take-up of such initiatives will be low, citing SkillsFuture credits left to the final months and not fully taken up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: My concern, however, is that the take-up rate for such initiatives will not be as high as desired, given what we have seen with the SkillsFuture credits where many people left it to the final months, and even then, it was not fully taken up.

sections.label: Expanding SG Digital Community Hubs
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether IMDA's SG Digital Community Hubs can be expanded to help seniors and more Singaporeans gain AI skills and safety tips.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Can the Infocomm Media Development Authority's (IMDA’s) SG Digital Community Hubs be expanded to help seniors and more Singaporeans gain AI skills and pick up safety tips?

sections.label: AI resources and career guidance
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to make AI resources more accessible, expand SG Digital Community Hubs for seniors, and provide stronger career guidance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, I am concerned about the potential low take-up as with SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to make AI resources more easily accessible, expand SG Digital Community Hubs to help seniors and providing stronger career guidance.

sections.label: Medium-term fiscal projections paper
sections.summary: MOF's 2023 Occasional Paper on Medium-Term Fiscal Projections signals total spending will rise to around 19.5% of GDP by 2030, driven by healthcare for an ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: MOF's Occasional Paper on Medium-Term Fiscal Projections in 2023 sends a very clear signal – our total spending will go up to around 19.5% of gross domestic product (GDP) by 2030, driven by healthcare for an ageing population.

sections.label: Budget 2026 revenue milestone
sections.summary: Budget 2026 is the first Budget since the Occasional Paper to reach 19.5% of GDP in total revenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Budget 2026 is a milestone in the sense that it is the first Budget since the Occasional Paper to hit that 19.5% of GDP in total revenues.

sections.label: GST rate and collection
sections.summary: GST collection rose from around 2% of GDP to 2.6% in Budget 2026 with the headline GST rate increase from 7% to 9%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: With the increase in headline GST rate from 7% to 9%, GST collection has gone up from around 2% of GDP to 2.6% in Budget 2026.

sections.label: Property tax and stamp duty
sections.summary: The speaker proposes raising property tax collections to 1.2% of GDP and making stamp duty more progressive, with a 15% tier above $5 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: But not too long ago, in the early 2000s, property tax collections were as high as 1% to 1.1% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: I think we should aim to raise property tax collections to 1.2% of GDP in the long term and focus on the top tier of residential properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Stamp duty collections stand at 0.8% of GDP in Budget 2026 and have largely been so for the past 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: I think we should make stamp duty much more progressive in the long term with, for example, a new tier for residential properties above $5 million, at marginal rate of 15%, 2.5 times the current top marginal rate.

sections.label: Deficit to fight crisis
sections.summary: A deficit of $51.6 billion, 10.8% of GDP, to fight the crisis of a generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: A deficit of $51.6 billion, 10.8% of GDP, to fight the crisis of a generation.

sections.label: Surpluses called modest
sections.summary: The speaker calls the FY2025 surplus of 1.9% of GDP and FY2026 surplus of 1% of GDP modest, citing FY2000's 2.4% surplus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: And further back, in FY2000, we had a surplus of 2.4% of GDP, although it was just $4 billion in dollar terms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: And so, in my view, the surplus for FY2025 at 1.9% of GDP is somewhat modest, hardly the greatest fiscal surplus any PAP Government has seen in decades; and the surplus for FY2026 at 1% of GDP is decidedly modest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: The accumulated surplus over the last term of Government, including the surplus for FY2025, is at around 0.6% of cumulative GDP, again, decidedly modest in my view.

sections.label: Surpluses over 26 years
sections.summary: Over the last 26 years, surpluses occurred in only 11 years, including FY2024 and FY2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Over the last 26 years, we have had surpluses in only 11 years, including FY2024 and FY2025.

sections.label: Extend GST offsets
sections.summary: Plough back part of the surpluses to extend transitional GST offsets by one more year for the vast majority of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Plough back part of the surpluses to extend our transitional GST offsets by one more year for the vast majority of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Balance, saving and sharing
sections.summary: The speaker says their idea of balance concerned societal spending and saving, and they combined two versions of a line after Minister of State Jasmin Lau's exhortation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: My idea of balance that I prompted you on was not so much about keeping versus sharing at the individual level, but about spending and saving at the societal level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Take only what is needed, leave the rest as sustenance for God's nature".

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: But I really liked the second line from the first version, so responding to the Minister of State Jasmin Lau's exhortation yesterday, I exercised my human agency and critical thinking, and I combined the two versions.

sections.label: FY2021 surplus and FY2023 deficit
sections.summary: The speaker states the FY2021 surplus was 0.3% of GDP and the FY2023 deficit 0.4% of GDP, which they took as largely balanced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: The surplus that we had for FY2021 was just 0.3% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: In FY2023, we had a deficit of 0.4% of GDP – and I took those to be largely balanced.

sections.label: MOF paper and GST revenue
sections.summary: The speaker cites the 2023 MOF Occasional Paper saying total spending needs will reach 19% to 20% of GDP by 2030, and says GST yields 0.6% of GDP more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: For the first, I would say, let us go back to the MOF Occasional Paper published in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: And it is stated very clearly in that paper that our total spending needs will hit 19% to 20% of GDP by 2030; the midpoint is 19.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: If the Member had listened to my speech and looked at the data, GST even with the increase from 7% to 9% headline rate, is yielding 0.6% of GDP more revenues – from 2% to 2.6% in this Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: GST alone hardly covers us up to the 19.5% target.

sections.label: Healthier society beyond wealth
sections.summary: The speaker says they spoke in Parliament about togetherness beyond early nationhood and that Singapore must be a healthier society, not simply a wealthier one.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: During the opening of Parliament, I spoke about the importance of us together and the role I hope to see us take as we move forward beyond early nationhood.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We must make Singapore a healthier society to live in, rather than simply a wealthier one.

sections.label: 6.9 million population parameter
sections.summary: The speaker says the ruling party uses 6.9 million as a population planning parameter and should explain the limit in the population plan.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Since the ruling party uses 6.9 million as a population planning parameter, they should at least give Singaporeans an explanation – what exactly is the limit in the population plan?

sections.label: Government reply on 6.9 million
sections.summary: The speaker says the Government told Aljunied MP Fadli Fawzi that 6.9 million remains a relevant planning parameter for the 2030s, with population size depending on trends and needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Government last month said in response to Aljunied MP Fadli Fawzi's question that, while the oft quoted number of 6.9 million is still a relevant planning parameter for the 2030s, our population size, not limits, depend on demographic trends and social and economic needs.

sections.label: Population projections and crowding research
sections.summary: A question asks if the Government would release regional population projections, citing research on perceived control in high density environments.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To relieve concerns, would the Government consider releasing population projections for each region as part of the Urban Redevelopment Authority's plans?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Research on perceived control in high density environments finds that stress responses are less affected by the actual density of the environment, but more on whether people believe that the crowding itself is being managed.

sections.label: Beijing licence plate lottery births
sections.summary: A 2018 Journal of Development Economics study found Beijing's vehicle licence plate lottery was associated with fewer births among participants and citywide.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For instance, research published in the Journal of Development Economics in 2018 found that the Beijing vehicle licence plate lottery system was associated with a 35% reduction in births in households of lottery participants and a 6% reduction in births across the entire city.

sections.label: Domestic worker rest days and HSS
sections.summary: A 2021 rule requires employers to give domestic workers one non-compensable rest day monthly, and the passage asks about assessments and HSS childminding changes.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2021, a rule was introduced, requiring employers to provide domestic workers at least one rest day a month that cannot be compensated away.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Has the Government more recently assessed if it is enough?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: With basic childminding services no longer being supported with manpower concessions under the HSS pilot from next month, is the Government working with providers to raise awareness of more general HSS services under the scheme?

sections.label: HDB free Sunday parking scheme
sections.summary: The passage states HDB's free parking scheme on Sundays and public holidays aims to promote social integration and stronger family ties.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In fact, it appears that some Government policies already take similar concerns into account, such as HDB's free parking scheme on Sundays and public holidays, which aims to promote social integration and stronger family ties.

sections.label: Select Committee on ban study
sections.summary: The passage says Australia's laws took effect in December and calls for a Select Committee to study whether a ban is appropriate.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Australia's laws came into effect in December last year, with countries like Spain, India, Denmark, Norway, Malaysia and the UK announcing similar intentions.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is time for Singapore to take clearer scientifically informed interventions to address these concerns.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This should include setting up a Select Committee to study whether a ban is appropriate in par in parallel to the Government's ongoing study and engagement with counterparts.

sections.label: Millennials survey on AI human touch
sections.summary: A Millennials Insights Survey found 43% of respondents were concerned extensive AI use might cause a loss of human touch.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Forty-three percent of respondents to a Millennials Insights Survey from last year were concerned that the extensive use of AI in their daily lives might result in a loss of human touch.

sections.label: AI overuse brain study
sections.summary: A study last year by MIT Media Lab found that over reliance on AI may reduce functional brain connectivity and memory recall.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While various MOE frameworks are in place, a study last year by MIT Media Lab found that over reliance on AI may reduce functional brain connectivity and memory recall.

sections.label: Protected nature areas legal boundaries
sections.summary: A 2024 Singapore Terrestrial Conservation Plan calls for the Government to set clear legal boundaries for protected nature areas and protect remaining habitats.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As called for in a 2024 Singapore Terrestrial Conservation Plan, the Government should establish clear legal boundaries for protected nature areas and protect the few remaining habitats that we have, which are absolutely key for both planetary and societal health.

sections.label: Southeast Asia per capita income
sections.summary: In 2024 Singapore is second in Southeast Asia per capita at about US$22,000, ahead of Malaysia, Thailand and the regional average, and 24th of 41 OECD entries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: In Southeast Asia, on a per capita basis, we are number two in 2024, at about US$22,000 per capita, behind Brunei.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: We are ahead of Malaysia which is about US$10,000; Thailand, about US$5,500; and the Southeast Asia average of about US$3,500 and we are close to the OECD average of about US$23,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Compared to OECD countries, Singapore sits around the mid-pack, 24th out of 41 entries.

sections.label: Retraining, fitness, CPF rates
sections.summary: The Government must keep people fit to work, acquire skills and grow retirement savings through compulsory retraining, fitness and higher CPF contribution rates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: The Government must keep our people fit to work, acquire relevant skills and grow their retirement nest egg.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: So, we need to do three things: one, compulsory retraining and skill upgrade every 10 years; two, staying physically and mentally fit to work; and three, increase forced savings rate or CPF contribution rates.

sections.label: MOM MTI MOE collaboration retraining
sections.summary: MOM, MTI and MOE must collaborate to close gaps between industry needs, job projections and retraining courses, with funding for workers at 40, 50 and 60.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: MOM, the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) and MOE must collaborate more closely to close the gap between industry needs in high-growth sectors, jobs projections and retraining or re-education courses, for example in sustainability, healthcare and information technology (IT).

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: I ask for the Government to consider funding workers for retraining or reskilling for every worker reaching 40, 50 and 60 for six months.

sections.label: Healthy SG, sabbaticals, working
sections.summary: One should press on with Healthy SG for those 40 and above, consider returning to school every 10 years, and view working as staying relevant rather than retiring early.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: First, we ought to press on with Healthy SG for those aged 40 and above.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Second, consider going back to school every 10 years, which is also a sabbatical from work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Last and most importantly, view working as a way of staying relevant, engage with community rather than retiring early.

sections.label: CPF contribution and interest rates
sections.summary: The passage asks whether higher CPF contribution rates and higher Ordinary and Special Account interest rates should be considered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: First, with more use of the funds in the Ordinary Account for property purchases, we may need to consider higher CPF contribution rate from employer and employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Second, can the CPF Board consider increasing the interest rate of 2.8% for the Ordinary Account and 4% for the Special Account?

sections.label: Institutionalising employee retraining
sections.summary: The passage proposes institutionalising retraining, such as training every 10 years, with Government subsidies and closer alignment between education and market demands.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Every employee is an important link in the chain.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: We should seriously consider institutionalising retraining arrangement, for example, allowing an employee to undergo training every 10 years, promoting closer alignment between the education system and market demands with appropriate Government subsidies to establish a more comprehensive retraining system, thereby maintaining employees' employability.

sections.label: Urgency over young seniors
sections.summary: The passage states urgency is needed or young seniors will become a lost generation needing long-term Government support, which vouchers and subsidies cannot solve.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Urgency because otherwise, the young seniors will become a "lost generation", which the Singapore Government will need to support for the long term.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: No amount of CDC vouchers and subsidies would help us tackle this problem.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: The tide of discontent is borne out of uncertainty and fear about the changes that await us.

sections.label: Political will to transform discontent
sections.summary: The passage calls for political will, courage and urgency to transform discontent into hope and remake the country and people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Let us find within us the political will, the courage and the great urgency to transform discontent into hope and ability to remake our country and our people to meet the challenges ahead.

sections.label: SSG and WSG merger
sections.summary: The passage states that SSG and WSG will merge into a single agency jointly overseen by MOM and MOE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SSG and WSG will merge into a single agency, jointly overseen by MOM and MOE.

sections.label: 2025 training participation figures
sections.summary: The passage states that in 2025, 606,000 individuals participated in SSG-supported training and 123,000 enrolled in courses with direct employability outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2025 alone, 606,000 individuals participated in SSG-supported training, and 123,000 enrolled in courses with direct employability outcomes.

sections.label: Retrenchments rose in 2025
sections.summary: Retrenchments rose to 14,400 in 2025 amid a choppy global outlook.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Retrenchments rose to 14,400 in 2025, on the back of a choppy global outlook.

sections.label: Permanent jobs and fixed term contracts
sections.summary: Over 90% of resident employees are in permanent jobs, around 7% remain on fixed term contracts, with older workers disproportionately on one-year contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the share declined slightly in 2025, with over 90% of resident employees now in permanent jobs, around 7% remain on fixed term contracts and older workers are disproportionately represented among one-year contracts.

sections.label: Working beyond official hours
sections.summary: Surveys show over 90% of employees worked beyond official hours, with 71% fearing negative repercussions for not responding after hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Surveys show over 90% of employees have worked beyond official hours, with 71% fearing negative repercussions if they do not respond after hours.

sections.label: CPF increases and investment scheme
sections.summary: Planned CPF contribution increases for senior workers proceed from January 2027 with a transition offset, and CPF will pilot a simplified investment scheme by 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The next step of planned CPF contribution increases for senior workers will proceed from January 2027, with a transition offset to help employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: CPF will also pilot a new simplified, low cost, life-cycle investment scheme by 2028 to give members more diversified options above the base interest rates.

sections.label: Training leave and contract pathways
sections.summary: Negotiated training leave must spread to non-union and SME settings, and the Public Service can catalyse norms through dashboards and clearer pathways from fixed term to permanent posts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Where unions are present, we have negotiated training leave into collective agreements; this must be spread by example into non-union and SME settings, with redesigned shifts, modular stackable courses and just-in-time learning aligned to job redesign.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Public Service can catalyse norms through transparent dashboards on contract renewal patterns and clearer pathways from fixed term contracts to permanent posts when work is ongoing.

sections.label: Budget 2026 household support
sections.summary: Families will still feel Budget 2026's support: cash Cost-of-Living Special Payments, enhanced U-Save rebates and CDC vouchers in January 2027.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Families will still feel Budget 2026's tangible support: cash Cost-of-Living Special Payments, enhanced U-Save rebates and CDC vouchers for all households in January 2027.

sections.label: Budget cost of living measures
sections.summary: The Budget makes long-term commitments on AI, business costs, enterprise ecosystem, public listings and the equity market, despite a 1.9% of GDP surplus.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: On the cost of living, I appreciate that this year's Budget is for the long game, long term, long run – intentional commitments to levelling up how we harness AI as a strategic advantage, supporting our local companies to manage business costs and build a regional and global footprint, as well as strengthening our enterprise ecosystem to support public listings and to develop the equity market.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Some sought clarification – why a healthy surplus to the tune of 1.9% of GDP has not already translated to more support measures.

sections.label: Reviewing revenue measures and taxes
sections.summary: The member asks whether the Government would re-time or review planned revenue-generating measures or taxes to ease cost-of-living pressures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: My question is, would the Government consider re-timing or reviewing planned revenue generating measures or taxes in the next few years, especially ones which may directly lead to alleviating cost-of-living pressures?

sections.label: Preschool and student care subsidies
sections.summary: The monthly household income threshold for preschool subsidies rises to $15,000 and for Student Care Fee Assistance to $6,500.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: The upwards review of monthly household income threshold to $15,000 for preschool subsidies means help reaches more lower- and middle-income households.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Similarly, the household income revision for Student Care Fee Assistance to $6,500 enhances access to after-school care, where students get the guidance they need and working parents get the support they deserve.

sections.label: Support for persons with disabilities
sections.summary: The member welcomes the Prime Minister's announcement that disability support is a key priority and awaits the task force's recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Speaker, Sir, I welcome Prime Minister Wong's announcement that strengthening support for persons with disabilities is a key priority of the Government and I look forward to the recommendations from the task force that will be reviewing how Singapore can provide more meaningful support at different life stages for persons with disabilities and their families.

sections.label: Social mobility and ComLink+
sections.summary: An Occasional Paper shows social mobility moderating; ComLink+ gets an additional $500 payout and interim findings are sought.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: The recent Occasional Paper on Income Growth, Inequality and Mobility Trends in Singapore revealed that while Singapore has done relatively well in sustaining social mobility compared to other advanced economies, our social mobility has shown signs of gradual moderation as Singapore's economy continue to mature and develop.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: One of Singapore's efforts to tackle social mobility is the ComLink+ programme, which will see an additional $500 payout for families working towards their milestone goals in this year's Budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: As the scheme was first launched in 2023 it is timely for the Government to share meaningful interim findings on how ComLink+ is beginning to translate into better educational and social outcomes for the children.

sections.label: Upstream AI intervention
sections.summary: The passage states that to level the playing field and access, AI intervention has to come upstream.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: To level the playing field and access, AI intervention has to come upstream.

sections.label: AI workforce safeguards and toolkits
sections.summary: Asks what safeguards prevent AI from replacing individuals or widening skill and income gaps, and suggests sector-specific AI toolkits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: What safeguards are in place to ensure AI does not inadvertently replace individuals or widen skill and income gaps in the workforce?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Perhaps the Government could consider collaborating with various key industries to create sector-specific AI toolkits, so talents can effectively conquer AI in their domains.

sections.label: CPF support for seniors
sections.summary: Notes higher CPF rates in 2027 and more investment options help young seniors, but asks how older seniors can contribute.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: For the young seniors, the planned increase in CPF contribution rates for senior workers in 2027 is helpful for retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Providing more investment options for CPF members also offers seniors the opportunity to grow assets, enabling them to age without worry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: But this must come with guardrails and capital preservation at the front and center.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: However, for older seniors who may face re-employment difficulties or are medically unfit, how will the Government support meaning contributions to their CPF accounts, so that the policy achieves its intended effect?

sections.label: Protections for platform workers
sections.summary: States that the last term strengthened platform worker protections, advanced progressive wages and made flexible work arrangements a workplace conversation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: In the last term, we strengthened protections for platform workers, advanced progressive wages and made Flexible Work Arrangements a legitimate workplace conversation.

sections.label: Flexible work request guidelines
sections.summary: States the Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests have been in place over a year, yet over half of surveyed workers never made a request.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: The Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests have been in place for more than a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Yet in our NTUC Women and Families surveys, more than half of workers have never made a request.

sections.label: Flexible and extended childcare options
sections.summary: Calls for childcare hours to reflect workforce realities and for expanded flexible and extended childcare, including weekend and after-hours pilots.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Childcare operating hours, especially in estates with shift workers, must better reflect workforce realities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: I therefore call for support to expand flexible and extended childcare options, including weekend and after-hours pilots in selected communities.

sections.label: NTUC women and workplace calls
sections.summary: Lists NTUC Women and Family efforts on lactation spaces and calls on Government to scale job redesign, benchmark workplaces, publish benchmarks, expand childcare and guide on menopause.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: The NTUC Women and Family unit will continue to promote lactational spaces in workplaces and we will continue to expand our NTUC Better Workplaces programme this year to support more companies with their lactation room set-ups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: I call on the Government to: scale job redesign funding and build expertise, especially in non-office based, frontline and shift-based sectors; recognise and benchmark progressive workplaces so inclusivity becomes part of Singapore’s competitive edge; publish sectoral benchmarks on FWA utilisation and career progression outcomes; expand flexible and extended childcare options; provide clearer tripartite guidance on supporting women through perimenopause and menopause as legitimate workplace health matters.

sections.label: Normalising flexible work arrangements
sections.summary: It says flexible work must be normalised as a workplace standard with funding, resourcing, hiring, job design, leadership KPIs and culture.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: It must not remain something that companies aspire to do just once a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: It must be normalised as a workplace standard with adequate funding and resourcing, embedded into hiring practices, job design, leadership key performance indicators and organisational culture.

sections.label: Reasonable accommodations for disabilities
sections.summary: It says NTUC secured stronger protections against workplace discrimination and tripartite partners are working on a Tripartite Advisory on Reasonable Accommodations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Apart from FWAs, NTUC has secured stronger protections against workplace discrimination and I am glad that this helps to level the playing field for our working persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: We are also working with tripartite partners on a Tripartite Advisory on Reasonable Accommodations to provide guidance on good practices that employers can adopt to make their workplaces more inclusive for persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: I call for clear guidance and appropriate funding under the upcoming tripartite advisory, so that our employers can implement inclusive practices confidently.

sections.label: Analysing job structures for AI
sections.summary: It calls on the Government to invest resources in analysing job structures, identifying AI-assisted and human functions, and designing training pathways.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: If we do not understand the true content of job roles, we may make the wrong judgement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Therefore, I call upon the Government to invest more resources in analysing job structures of various industries, clearly identify which functions can be assisted by AI and which must be completed by humans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Then, based on real circumstances, design training and transformation pathways.

sections.label: Youths worried about finding jobs
sections.summary: It states that last year a quarter of youths from IHLs polled in NTUC's Youth Employment Outlook worried about finding a job within six months of graduation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: Last year, a quarter of our youths from our IHLs, polled in NTUC's Youth Employment Outlook, expressed worries about finding a job within six months of graduation.

sections.label: Younger workers' AI job risk
sections.summary: It states NTUC's 2025 survey found 19% of younger workers saw technology or AI as the greatest job risk, and 53% recognised upskilling needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: From the NTUC Survey on Economic Sentiments in 2025, the perception that technology or AI will be the greatest risk to their jobs in the next year was highest among younger workers – 19% compared to the average of 16%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: And 53% of younger workers, more than any other age group, recognise the need to upskill to stay relevant even if they could keep their job.

sections.label: AI boosted customer support productivity
sections.summary: It cites 2023/2024 National Bureau of Economic Research studying 5,000 customer support agents finding AI assistance significantly boosted productivity, especially for less experienced workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: Research from a 2023/2024 National Bureau of Economic Research, studying 5,000 customer support agents found that AI assistance significantly boosted productivity, especially for less experienced workers.

sections.label: AI weakens junior hiring incentive
sections.summary: If AI can do training and learning tasks faster and cheaper, the short-term economic incentive to hire juniors weakens.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: If AI can perform the training task, the learning task faster and cheaper, the short-term economic incentive to hire juniors weakens.

sections.label: Missing middle in Singapore
sections.summary: Entry level jobs might not be available in the same number over time, worsening hollowing out of Singaporean middle management and risking a missing middle.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: However, this also means that entry level jobs might not be available in the same number over time and this might worsen the hollowing out of the Singaporean middle management.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: We risk, what I call a missing middle.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: Powerful algorithms, a thin layer of senior experts and too few local managers and specialists in between.

sections.label: New industrial policy for entry jobs
sections.summary: The solution to the broken rung is to create a new one, requiring a new industrial policy for entry level jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: Instead, the solution to the broken rung is not to repair the old one, it is to create a new one.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: We need a new industrial policy for entry level jobs.

sections.label: Government co-funding hiring gap
sections.summary: Government can co-fund part of that gap for a defined period, de-risking the hiring decision while building national capability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: Government can co-fund part of that gap for a defined period, de-risking the hiring decision while building national capability.

sections.label: Graduates proficient in practical AI
sections.summary: Every graduate should be proficient not only in theory but in practical AI usage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: Every graduate should be proficient, not only in theory, but in practical AI usage.

sections.label: Early training access and Place and Train
sections.summary: SkillsFuture credits are accessible later in a worker's career, but AI compresses learning and skill cycles, so early access to training support should be examined and Place and Train opportunities expanded.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: Under current arrangements, SkillsFuture credits are accessible later in a worker's career, but AI compresses learning and skill cycles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: In fact, many of our current graduates might already need to complement their academic training while in school to be ready for the new workforce demands.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: We should examine whether early access to training support might be needed in this new environment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: At the same time, we must expand Place and Train opportunities and career bridges models.

sections.label: Innovation and missing middle
sections.summary: Warns that without innovating ahead of time, there is a risk of a missing middle crisis and a hollowed out workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: If we do not innovate ahead of time, we risk a missing middle crisis, a hollowed out workforce.

sections.label: Childhood LifeSG Credits gap
sections.summary: Budget 2026 gives $500 Childhood LifeSG Credits to Singaporean children aged 12 and below, but no equivalent measures for families with older children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Budget 2026 provides $500 in Childhood LifeSG Credits for every Singaporean child aged 12 and below.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: They are meaningful and a welcomed form of support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But Budget 2026 contains no equivalent measures for families with children who have moved beyond primary school.

sections.label: Flexible support age limit
sections.summary: Asks the Ministry to clarify whether limiting flexible support to children aged 12 and below was conscious or an unrevised gap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Budget 2026 provides flexible relief for one cohort of families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I invite the Ministry to clarify whether it was a conscious decision to limit flexible support to children aged 12 and below, leaving families with older children without an equivalent, or whether this gap has simply not been revisited as family expenses have evolved.

sections.label: ComLink+ eligible families estimate
sections.summary: States the population is smaller than total rental housing stock but larger than 10,000, and asks for the Ministry's estimate of families eligible for ComLink+.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: That population is smaller than the total rental housing stock, but it is significantly larger than 10,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I would ask the Minister to share what is the Ministry's estimates as the total number of families eligible for ComLink+ under its current criteria.

sections.label: Eligible families not served
sections.summary: Requests the current number of eligible families not yet served by ComLink+.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, to state the current number of eligible families not yet served by ComLink+.

sections.label: Preschool subsidy income ceilings
sections.summary: States higher income ceilings for preschool subsidies and student care fee assistance, and notes a family earning $13,500 still pays more than it should for nine months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The monthly household income ceiling for preschool subsidies will rise from $12,000 to $15,000, benefiting more than 60,000 additional families and the student care fee assistance ceiling will rise from $4,500 to $6,500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I also note that the reduction in fee caps for both anchor operator and partner operator preschools, which took effect in January 2026, already provides some interim relief to middle-income families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But even accounting for that, a family earning $13,500 a month above today's subsidy ceiling and below the incoming one is still paying more than they should be for another nine months.

sections.label: Family coach programme coverage
sections.summary: A proactive family coach programme covers about 10,000 public rental families, far fewer than eligible, and Budget 2026 does not state targets to expand coaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One method is by using a proactive family coach to help low-income families living in public rental flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, so far, this programme only involves approximately 10,000 families, whereas the number of eligible families is far greater.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Budget 2026 increases the support package for families that are already in this programme but does not state any targets or plans to increase the number and the training of coaches.

sections.label: Support delivery asks and marriage decline
sections.summary: The speaker asks for a published review, a ComLink+ coverage target and coach plan, and an explanation why April 2026 is not feasible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Every family the Government has acknowledged as deserving support through fee cap reduction, through expanded subsidy thresholds and through ComLink+ design, should receive that support well with predictability, without arbitrary age cut-offs, without a nine-month gap between announcement and delivery, and not only if they happen to be among the 10,000 families with a coach already assigned to them, The three asks I have made today are specific and proportionate, a published review of whether the structure of support for families with post-primary school age children is well matched to the cost they actually bear; a stated coverage target and coach investment plan for ComLink+; and for the last point, an explanation on why April 2026 is not feasible as a start date, and if the gap cannot be closed, a transitional bridging measure from families who are caught waiting using instruments that the Government has deployed before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Just this week, The Straits Times reported that 2025 recorded the lowest number of marriages in Singapore since 2020, a third consecutive year of decline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Researchers point to longer-term shifts in how Singaporeans perceive marriage, but also to concerns that policy can more directly speak to – uncertain economic future, a higher cost of living and the need to be financially stable before starting a family.

sections.label: Combined effect of support gaps
sections.summary: Age cut-offs, limited programme reach and delayed subsidy expansions may together reinforce the hesitation policy should reduce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Flexible support that falls off at age cut-offs, programmes whose reach falls short of eligible need and subsidy expansions that arrive later than necessary may each appear defensible in isolation, but taken together, they risk reinforcing the very hesitation that policy design should be working to reduce, not entrench.

sections.label: Budget corporate tax rebate
sections.summary: The Budget includes a 40% tax rebate and a $1,500 benefit for active companies with at least one local employee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Budget includes a tax rebate of 40% and the benefit of $1,500 for active companies with at least one local employee.

sections.label: Support for micro and home-based businesses
sections.summary: The speaker proposes extending support to micro and home-based businesses, noting SMCCI engaged 1,800 such businesses during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, I would like to propose that the Government extends support to micro and home-based businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: During the pandemic, the Singapore Malay Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SMCCI) engaged with 1,800 home-based businesses which embody the spirit of entrepreneurship and have shown resilience in managing their operations.

sections.label: Grants for business missions
sections.summary: The speaker proposes enhanced grants for trade associations, chambers and SMEs to facilitate regular business missions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Financial support plays a vital role in this expansion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I propose that enhanced grant be provided to trade associations and chambers and SMEs to facilitate regular business missions.

sections.label: Free trade agreements and ASEAN
sections.summary: Establishing more FTAs and strengthening ASEAN partnerships, including the Johor-Singapore SEZ, will ensure local companies are welcome in the region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Establishing more free trade agreements (FTAs) and strengthening our partnership with ASEAN partners, such as the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (SEZ), and various other countries will ensure our local companies are welcome in the region and do extremely well via partnership or even merger and acquisition.

sections.label: Business missions abroad
sections.summary: The speaker participated in and led business missions organised by SMCCI, SBF, Enterprise Singapore and the UAE Singapore Business Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I have also participated and at times led numerous business missions organised by SMCCI, SBF, Enterprise Singapore and the UAE Singapore Business Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These missions are crucial for companies to receive support, minimise errors in establishing their business in foreign markets and gain access to the robust network developed by Enterprise Singapore and trade associations and chambers.

sections.label: Emerging new industries
sections.summary: New industries such as space technology, advanced manufacturing, data centres and renewable energy are emerging and offer employment opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: New industries such as space technology, advanced manufacturing, utilisation, data centres and renewable energy are emerging, offering a wide range of employment opportunities.

sections.label: Data-driven family support
sections.summary: Support for Singapore families should move to a data-driven model calibrated on household dependency ratios so those needing most help receive it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On providing support for Singapore families, we must also move towards a more sophisticated, data-driven model of support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We know that a family in a 3-room flat caring for a special needs child or an ailing octogenarian faces vastly different pressures than a young couple in the same block.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am confident with the data that we have, the support should be calibrated based on household dependency ratios to ensure that those who need the most help receive it regularly until they can truly fend for themselves.

sections.label: Keeping Singapore Dream alive
sections.summary: Strengthening the economy, companies, global outreach, workforce careers and family support ensures the Singapore Dream remains a living reality for all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By strengthening our economy, companies, global outreach, respected career for our workforce and refining our family support, we ensure that the Singapore Dream remains a living reality for all.

sections.label: Household income growth percentiles
sections.summary: Real household income per member grew by 3.1% for the bottom 20th percentile, compared with 2.9% for the median.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Real household income per member grew by 3.1% for the bottom 20th percentile, compared with 2.9% for the median.

sections.label: Real income growth percentiles
sections.summary: Between 2024 and 2025, real income grew 3.6% at the 20th percentile and 4.1% at the median.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Between 2024 and 2025, real income grew by 3.6% at the 20th percentile, but 4.1% at the median.

sections.label: Local Qualifying Salary increase
sections.summary: The Government raised the Local Qualifying Salary from $1,600 to $1,800 in Budget 2026, roughly the 2023 10th percentile wage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Last September, I called for the Local Qualifying Salary to be raised in this term of Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I therefore thank the Government for responding in Budget 2026 by increasing the Local Qualifying Salary from $1,600 to $1,800.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: A Local Qualifying Salary of $1,800 corresponds roughly to the 10th percentile wage in nominal terms in 2023 – some three years ago.

sections.label: PWM workers leave entitlement
sections.summary: Leave for PWM workers in outsourced sectors stagnates at seven days, so the Government is called on to raise it to 10 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: As a result, their leave stagnates at the statutory minimum of seven days, despite years of service in the same job scope.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I therefore call on the Government to raise the baseline leave entitlement for PWM workers in outsourced sectors from seven days to 10 days.

sections.label: PWM in pest management
sections.summary: NTUC engaged the Singapore Pest Management Association and industry stakeholders to implement PWM in the pest management sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: For example, in the pest management sector, NTUC has engaged the Singapore Pest Management Association and industry stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: We hope to implement PWM in this sector to professionalise the industry, improve retention and build local talent pipelines.

sections.label: SkillsFuture worker-centric shift
sections.summary: SkillsFuture must shift from course-centric to worker-centric, integrated with NTUC's AI-powered Career Coach to deliver personalised training pathways.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: SkillsFuture must therefore shift from being course-centric to worker-centric.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: SkillsFuture can be integrated with NTUC’s AI-powered Career Coach to deliver personalised training pathways at scale – identifying skills gaps, recommending relevant courses and mapping out progression pathways.

sections.label: NTUC Care Fund support
sections.summary: In 2025, the NTUC Care Fund supported over 47,000 lower-income union members and families, disbursing close to $5.5 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In 2025 alone, the NTUC Care Fund supported over 47,000 lower-income union members and their families through various Care Assistance Programmes, with close to $5.5 million disbursed.

sections.label: AI rise and workers
sections.summary: Calls for Singapore to rise together in the age of AI, leaving no worker behind and carrying every family forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: So, let us ensure that as Singapore rises in the age of AI, we rise together, leaving no worker behind and carrying every family forward.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We are operating in a world that is more fragmented, less predictable, in a world where small missteps now carry larger consequences.

sections.label: Budget 2026 AI push
sections.summary: States that Budget 2026 accelerates Singapore's push in AI and other strategic capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Budget 2026 rightly accelerates Singapore's push in AI and other strategic capabilities.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and Workforce Singapore merger
sections.summary: Says merging SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore brings training and job placement under one roof, connecting skills upgrading to employment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The merger of SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore is significant because it brings training and job placement under one roof so that upgrading skills connects more directly to employment.

sections.label: Education spending and teachers
sections.summary: Says placing 21st century competencies at the heart of education requires change, with teachers central, and notes MOE expenditure increases.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But in doing so and placing the 21st century competencies at the heart of our national educational priorities, this will require significant change and teachers must be at the centre of this transformation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That is why I am encouraged that this Budget recognises the central role of education in securing our future, with MOE's total expenditure projected to increase by 8.8% year-on-year and operating expenditure rising by 6%, largely to recruit more educators.

sections.label: Higher education metrics and framework
sections.summary: Says transforming higher education for an AI-led world requires aligning institutional metrics, and Singapore can catalyse an international framework for universities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we are serious about transforming higher education for an AI-led world, then we must also align the metrics that institutions pay attention to.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore is well placed to catalyse the development of a complementary international framework for universities governed multilaterally by academics, policy-makers, industry and civil society.

sections.label: MCCY budget increase
sections.summary: Notes that the MCCY budget increased by 13.8% in Budget 2026, with much directed toward infrastructure development.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They generate both social capital and economic spillovers through events and the broader creative economy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, it is encouraging that the MCCY budget has increased by 13.8% in Budget 2026, with much of this increase directed toward infrastructure development.

sections.label: AI tax deductions and arts sports giving
sections.summary: Budget 2026 grants up to 400% tax deductions on qualified AI spend, and notes 2024 arts and sports donations, proposing stronger giving incentives.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Budget 2026 grants up to 400% tax deductions on qualified AI spend for businesses to catalyse innovation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2024, arts organisations raised about $45 million in cash and in-kind donations, roughly 3.3% of total giving, while sports organisations raised about $16.7 million, or 1.2% of total giving.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Strengthening incentives for sustained giving to qualified Institutions of a Public Character in the arts and sports would deepen participation and reinforce the practitioner base without significantly increasing public expenditure.

sections.label: Caregiving commitments and training time
sections.summary: Workers with financial commitments ask if they have time and money to learn, so the Government increased caregiving support and will review student care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This group has financial commitments: housing loans, caregiving responsibilities and children in school.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, when industries transform, they not only ask: "What should I learn?", but also "Do I have time to go and learn?", "Can I afford to make this move?" I therefore thank the Government for announcing increased support for aged care, preschool childcare and student care, and committing holistically to review the student care sector to better meet the caregiving needs of families with primary school-aged children.

sections.label: Training, guidance and job matching reform
sections.summary: Many were willing to learn but unsure of employment outcomes, and this structural reform improves coordination between training, career guidance and job matching.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Many were willing to learn, but unsure whether courses would translate into real employment outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This structural reform improves coordination between training, career guidance and most importantly, job matching.

sections.label: NTUC CTC Grant for company transformation
sections.summary: NTUC's CTC Grant funds structured transformation initiatives that directly translate into better worker outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: NTUC's CTC Grant supports companies in doing precisely this – by funding structured transformation initiatives that directly translate into better worker outcomes.

sections.label: Early union leader engagement in restructuring
sections.summary: Early engagement of union leaders before formal announcements allowed quiet preparations and advance identification of alternative employment options to reduce worker uncertainty.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: When union leaders were engaged early, even before formal announcements, preparations could begin quietly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Alternative employment options could be identified in advance to minimise the period of uncertainty for the worker.

sections.label: Frequent restructuring in AI age
sections.summary: As transitions accelerate in the age of AI, restructuring may become more frequent across many sectors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As transitions accelerate in the age of AI, restructuring may become more frequent across many sectors.

sections.label: Confidence-building in transition frameworks
sections.summary: Speaker suggests embedding confidence-building and structured activation support in transition frameworks alongside skills upgrading and job matching.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We have seen through structured activation and resilience interventions that when workers regain clarity and confidence, follow-through and interview rates, and transition outcomes improve.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I therefore suggest that confidence-building and structured activation support be intentionally embedded within our transition frameworks, alongside skills upgrading and job matching.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This could help integrate structured coaching and activation components into career conversion programmes and transition support services, so that workers receive not only technical training but guided momentum towards re-employment.

sections.label: Employment and employability partnerships
sections.summary: FA4 can strengthen employer and industry ties to create training, internships and placements, while NTUC's AI-Ready SG supports workers and entrepreneurs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In the areas of Employment and Employability, FA4 can continue to strengthen relations with employers and industry partners, so that more training opportunities, internships and job placements are created in the growth sectors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: On NTUC's part, through initiatives, like AI-Ready SG, we will continue to support workers and entrepreneurs in facing this change.

sections.label: Three foundations for worker transitions
sections.summary: Speaker says strengthening clarity, early trusted engagement and confidence will ensure transitions strengthen the workforce, citing OECD PISA and World Bank rankings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: (In English): Sir, in closing, as transitions become more frequent in the age of AI, our responsibility is clear.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We must strengthen clarity, so workers see the real pathways forward.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We must deepen early, trusted engagement, so no one feels blindsided by change.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And we must intentionally build confidence so that workers are equipped not only with skills but also with the self-assurance and resilience to move forward.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: If we get these three foundations right, transition will not weaken our workforce.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It will only strengthen it and Singapore will continue to move ahead with our workers, not ahead of them.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Our most recent ranking in the OECD PISA has us ranked first worldwide and the World Bank's Human Capital Index likewise has put us up top.

sections.label: Education and economic progress
