sections.summary: Years of schooling rose from under four in 1960 to over 12 by 2015, making public education the backbone of economic progress.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: The overall number of years of schooling in the population went from less than four years in 1960 to more than 12 by 2015, with an emphasis on science and technical education, coupled with a rigorous system of sorting and tracking, public education became the backbone of our nation's remarkable economic progress.

sections.label: AI compresses skills gap
sections.summary: Emerging research indicates AI compresses the skills gap by raising productivity of inexperienced and lesser trained workers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Emerging research already points to how AI compresses the skills gap by raising the productivity of inexperienced and lesser trained workers.

sections.label: Primary school class sizes
sections.summary: In primary schools, there are still classrooms with as many as 40 students.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: In primary schools, we still have classrooms that have as many as 40 students.

sections.label: Edtech as teacher complement
sections.summary: Edtech works when treated as a complement to teachers, which requires a better teacher-to-student ratio.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: The saving grace for such applications is that if they are applied in a thoughtful and deliberate manner, which occurs when edtech is treated as a compliment rather than a substitute for the teacher.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: This, in turn, calls for a better ratio of teachers to students in the classroom.

sections.label: High stakes exams relevance
sections.summary: Major high stakes examinations will be less relevant in an AI age.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Major high stakes examinations long, a mainstay of gauging student understanding and evaluating student performance, will be less relevant in an AI age.

sections.label: Examination weight in grading
sections.summary: Mid-year and final examinations could comprise up to four-fifths of the total grade, and abolishing mid-year exams without rebalancing assessment weights remains half-hearted.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Until recently, mid-year and final examinations could comprise as much as four-fifths of the total grade, which places an inordinate emphasis on these markers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: So, even though the Ministry formally abolished mid-year examinations three years ago without an accompanying rebalancing of the weight placed on examinations and tests versus other forms of assessment, the effort will always remain half-hearted.

sections.label: Frequent low-stake quizzes
sections.summary: Frequent low-stake quizzes, as much as once a day, can improve conceptual retention and understanding.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Frequent but low-stake quizzes, as much as once a day, can improve conceptual retention and understanding.

sections.label: Early tracking and inequality
sections.summary: Tracking too early, between ages 10 and 12, increases educational inequality without clear achievement gains.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Similarly, the evidence on tracking too early, by early, the literature suggests between the ages of 10 and 12, which incidentally, is precisely when we start subject-based banding and institute the PSLE, actually increases educational inequality without any clear achievement gains.

sections.label: GenAI and graduate hiring
sections.summary: GenAI and Agent AI can perform tasks new graduates used to fill, weakening firms' incentive to hire them.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: GenAI can easily synthesise and deliver information that all but the very best undergraduates struggle to absorb, relieving the need for entry level positions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Agent AI can already accurately execute a wide range of tasks that new graduates used to fill, which means that firms will have a far weaker incentive for hiring them.

sections.label: Youth unemployment rate trend
sections.summary: Youth unemployment remains below other advanced economies but has trended up since mid-2024.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Notably, while our youth unemployment rate remains considerably below those of other advanced economies, this has steadily trended up since the middle of 2024.

sections.label: Research innovation enterprise funding
sections.summary: Prime Minister Wong's $37 billion Research, Innovation and Enterprise funding is welcome, though national research and development spending still lacks comparable technologically forward economies.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Prime Minister Wong's $37 billion funding for the Research, Innovation and Enterprise plan is undeniably a welcome step, and if resource constraints were the only limitation to research success, we would be well positioned, even though, as I previously mentioned, our national research and development spending still lacks those of comparable technologically forward economies.

sections.label: Autonomous universities global rankings
sections.summary: Autonomous universities must stop chasing global rankings for their own sake and focus on genuine academic enterprise.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Our autonomous universities must stop chasing global rankings for their own sake, but instead focus on the genuine nature of academic enterprise, a point that Member Kenneth Goh, a fellow academic, has just made.

sections.label: AI, weaker students, educational diversity
sections.summary: AI will compress the talent gap and devalue traditional degrees, giving weaker students and those with undervalued skills a chance to shine.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Weaker students now have a more realistic chance than ever before to shine in the classroom.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Not only will AI compress the talent gap, it will devalue the traditional degree, which opens the door for those who, endowed with hitherto undervalued skills, to finally stake their place in the modern economy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: This includes those who may not be as book smart, but who are gifted in myriad other ways.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Those who are blessed with superior hand-eye coordination, or are more innately social, or exude practical intelligence, or possess a tinker's mentality.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Let us also embrace neurological and intellectual diversity, starting from the ground up with our educational system.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Let us allow diversity to be the core strength of our educational system in this AI age.

sentences.text: At Tan Tock Seng Hospital, the introduction of an AI-enabled predictive patient monitoring system has helped our nurses manage fall-risk patients more effectively.

sections.summary: The speaker calls on tripartite partners to step up support for senior workers to prevent premature exit from the workforce and sustain meaningful employment, saying the Budget lays foundations for an AI-enabled economy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: This Budget lays strong foundations for the transformation towards an AI-enabled economy.

sentences.text: I will propose specific measures during the COS, including grants for companies deploying Singaporeans to regional roles and work exposure programmes for young graduates in ASEAN markets.

sections.label: Support return to workforce
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to implement a scheme supporting return to the workforce for those who gave up career years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: They have given up some of the very best years of their careers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I call on the Government to implement a scheme to support their return to the workforce.

sections.label: Social enterprise employment mission
sections.summary: Mr Daniel Yeow of The Social Space shared that sustaining dignified employment for vulnerable groups is becoming much harder.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Mr Daniel Yeow, who runs The Social Space, a social enterprise in the F&B sector, shared with me that it is becoming much harder to sustain their mission of providing dignified employment to vulnerable groups, such as single parents with caregiving burdens, at-risk youths and people with mental health conditions.

sections.label: Take A Chance grant proposal
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Government to consider a Take A Chance grant for employers hiring vulnerable persons, similar to existing credit schemes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Yet it is challenging for such enterprises to fully benefit from the various AI and productivity related schemes in order to provide employment to such groups of people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I would like the Government to consider a "Take A Chance" grant for employers who hire such vulnerable persons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: There are already the Senior Employment Credit for hiring seniors, Enabling Employment Credit for hiring persons with disabilities and the Uplifting Employment Credit for hiring ex-offenders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We can introduce another similar credit scheme for employers who take a chance on persons from other vulnerable and marginalised groups and offer them meaningful long-term employment.

sections.label: Youth mental health statistics
sections.summary: About one-third of Singapore youths aged 15 to 35 reported severe depression, anxiety or stress symptoms, affecting school attendance and performance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In Singapore, about one-third of youths aged 15 to 35 reported severe or extremely severe symptoms of depression, anxiety or stress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Students dealing with these conditions miss about 190 hours – or 24 days – of school annually and mental health struggles cut down school performance by 63%.

sections.label: SG Partnerships Fund for youths
sections.summary: The Budget announced a $50 million SG Partnerships Fund to support more ground-up community initiatives for youths who want to build the nation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For youths who want to do more and who are not content to be mere spectators, but want to build our nation together, I see immense potential in the Budget announcement of a $50 million SG Partnerships Fund, so we can support more ground-up community initiatives.

sections.label: Bishan Community Club special needs initiative
sections.summary: The speaker is working on an initiative at Bishan Community Club to make it conducive for those with special needs, and started an initiative promoting bonding between parents, grandparents and children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: During the briefing, I learnt about how some parents keep their autistic children at home for fear of the social rejection they would encounter should their children go through a meltdown in public.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am working on an initiative in Bishan Community Club to make it a comfortable and conducive space for those with special needs, so they know they are welcome at our events.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We are doing this by setting aside calm corners, training volunteers to know how to engage such families and designing wayfinding features.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I also started an initiative to promote bonding between parents, grandparents and children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is an indoor space with loose parts free play, which is going to expand to serve children with special needs.

sections.label: Volunteer mother in rental flat
sections.summary: The speaker found an answer in a volunteer in the community, a young mother of an eight-year-old boy with hearing disabilities living in a rental flat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I found an answer in a volunteer in my community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: She is a young mother of an eight-year-old boy with hearing disabilities, and she lives with her family in a rental flat.

sections.label: Singapore investors in China
sections.summary: Singapore has for several years been China's largest foreign investors, with approximately 4,000 Singapore companies in Shanghai alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Despite our small domestic economy, Singapore has, for several years, been China's largest foreign investors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In Shanghai alone, there are approximately 4,000 Singapore companies there.

sections.label: Singapore-China bilateral ties and CSFTA
sections.summary: Bilateral ties between Singapore and China have deepened and expanded, with the CSFTA allowing most Singapore exports to China to enter tariff-free.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Over decades, bilateral ties between Singapore and China have deepened and expanded significantly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We have a comprehensive China-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (CSFTA) which allows the majority of our export to China to enter tariff-free.

sections.label: Singapore-Johore SEZ and FTAs
sections.summary: The Government is pushing for businesses to consider stepping up at the Singapore-Johore Special Economic Zone, and Singapore now has 28 implemental FTAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Government is also pushing for businesses to consider stepping up at the Singapore-Johore Special Economic Zone, which is a natural and logical move, given our proximity, our familiarity, as well as our complementarity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Singapore now has 28 implemental FTAs, including multilateral agreements, such as the ASEAN FTA, the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership, the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership.

sections.label: Overseas expansion funds welcomed
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the $1.5 billion Anchor Fund and $1.5 billion Financial Sector Development Fund announced in Budget 2026, noting overseas expansions carry risks and need patient capital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Overseas expansions carry significant risks and often demand patient capital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: So, I welcome the $1.5 billion Anchor Fund and $1.5 billion Financial Sector Development Fund announced in Budget 2026.

sections.label: Budget surpluses despite rising expenditure
sections.summary: The speaker asks how Singapore recorded a $15.1 billion surplus in FY2025 and a projected $8.5 billion surplus in FY2026 despite rising expenditures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: As the Budget debate is about financial policy of the Government, the elephant in the room question is of course how is it that despite rising expenditures over the years, Singapore recorded significant surplus of $15.1 billion in FY2025, with a projected $8.5 billion surplus in FY2026?

sections.label: Net Investment Returns Contribution increase
sections.summary: The second component is a $3.4 billion increase in the Net Investment Returns Contribution from FY2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The second component comes from the significant increase in the Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) – a hefty $3.4 billion from FY2024.

sections.label: Corporate income tax rise
sections.summary: Corporate income tax rose from $30.1 billion in FY2024 to $35.2 billion in FY2025 and is projected at $37.8 billion in FY2026, driven by growth and BEPS Pillar 2 taxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Corporate income tax rose from $30.1 billion from FY2024 to $35.2 billion in FY2025 – the revised figures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: And it is projected to rise to $37.8 billion in FY2026, an increase of roughly one-third over three years, driven by stronger-than-expected growth and the implementation of the BEPS Pillar 2 top-up taxes.

sections.label: Taxing rich and foreigners
sections.summary: The speaker asks why not tax the rich or foreigners more and distribute to lower- and middle-income households, citing strong fiscal position and prudent stewardship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Taken together, the lower- and the middle-income families effectively pays a GST rate that is 7% or below.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: So, I ask myself why would we not want to tax more from the rich or the foreigners who are here to spend more, and then use the financial resources to distribute it to the lower- and the middle-income households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: It is precisely because we remained in the position of physical strength that we are able to allocate meaningful resources across these three pillars: social development, economic growth and security in support of our long-term nation building.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Prudent stewardship over the years has provided the Government with the capacity not only to respond to immediate challenges but also to invest strategically in our collective future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Our strong fiscal position put us in good stead to confront emerging risks, seize new opportunities, safeguard Singapore's continued progress for generations to come.

sections.label: Benefits denied to unmarried parents
sections.summary: Children of unmarried parents do not receive the $11,000 Baby Bonus Cash Gift, are not recognised as a family nucleus for HDB schemes, and cannot claim the Parenthood Tax Rebate of up to $20,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: One, their unmarried parent does not receive the Baby Bonus Cash Gift of $11,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Two, they are not recognised as part of a "family nucleus" for HDB schemes, they receive lower subsidies than the family grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Three, their unmarried parent is excluded from the most substantive tax benefits we provide for families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: They cannot claim the Parenthood Tax Rebate of up to $20,000.

sections.label: Non-working mothers lack childcare subsidies
sections.summary: Non-working mothers currently do not qualify for additional subsidies for childcare and after-school care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Currently, non-working mothers do not qualify for the additional subsidies for childcare as well as after-school care.

sections.label: Extending subsidies, dropping working mother criteria
sections.summary: The speaker proposes granting additional childcare and after-school subsidies to all students and dropping the working mother criteria, including early intervention, special student care, and assistive technology subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Let us grant the additional subsidies for childcare and afterschool care to all students and drop the working mother criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Again, I do not believe that this will overnight make all of our working mothers wake up and decide to stop work, or this encourage those who are looking for work to not continue to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And this will include additional subsidy for the Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children, subsidies for Special Student Care Centres, subsidies for children who need assistive technology and devices, like hearing aids.

sections.label: Time spent in ASA process
sections.summary: At the point they came to the speaker, they had spent more than one and a half years since starting the ASA process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: At the point where theycame to me, they had spent more than one and a half years since they started the ASA process.

sections.label: Adoption wait, reassessment, shorter leave
sections.summary: The speaker questions waiting nine more months to start the process and reassessing adoption suitability when things go well with the first child, and notes adoption leave is 12 weeks versus 16 weeks maternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Why the need to wait another nine more months to start the process, and why then the need to reassess them for adoption suitability, when things are going well with the first child?

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And to compound the situation, compared to maternity leave of 16 weeks, adoption leave for parents is only 12 weeks.

sections.label: Streamlining adoption, extending subsidies, aligning leave
sections.summary: The speaker urges agencies to streamline the adoption process, extend Singapore Citizenship subsidies to the child on a Dependent's Pass, and align adoption leave with maternity leave at 16 weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: So, I urge all the relevant Government agencies and there are many involved in the process as I have described, to come together, work towards streamlining the process for parents significantly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And may I suggest that during the period where the child is in Singapore on a Dependent's Pass, let us extend the Singapore Citizenship subsidies for infant care, for childcare, for medicals to the child, because it is a matter of time that they will become a citizen, and these are critical developmental years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Let us not lose time and also let us align the adoption leave with maternity leave at 16 weeks.

sections.label: MOE PSLE and O-level results
sections.summary: MOE replied that for PSLE at least nine in 10 students achieved AL6 or better in English, Mother Tongue, Math and Science, and about nine in 10 obtained C6 or better at O levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: MOE replied that for PSLE, at least nine in 10 students achieved AL6 or better in English, Mother Tongue, Math and Science; and for the "O" levels, about nine in 10 obtain a C6 or better in English, Mother Tongue and Math.

sections.label: PISA 2022 top performers
sections.summary: In PISA 2022, 41% of Singapore students were top performers in Math, 24% in Science and 23% in reading, versus OECD's 9% and 7%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In the latest PISA 2022 assessment of 15-year-olds, 41% of our students were classified as top performers for Math, 24% for Science, and 23% for reading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In comparison, for the OECD, it was 9% classified top performers for Math, 7% each for Science and reading.

sections.label: National exam grades and top performers
sections.summary: If 40% of the cohort are top Math performers globally, then 40% should get the top or top two grades in Math.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: If 40% of our cohort are considered top performers in Math globally, then the performance on the national exams should reflect as such – 40% of the cohort should get the top or top two grades in Math.

sections.label: Role of national exams
sections.summary: The role of national exams should be to assess for competency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The role of national exams should be to assess for competency.

sections.label: Gen Z IQ and screen time
sections.summary: Studies suggest Gen Z may show lower average IQ and cognitive scores, linked to screen time, devices and social media, with AI compounding challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: Already, there have been studies that suggest that Gen Z may be the first generation that shows lower average intelligence quotient (IQ) and cognitive scores than previous generations for attention, memory and literacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: This is linked to screen time, digital devices and social media – and I have no doubt that AI will compound these challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: In this context, it becomes even more critical that our students achieve fundamental competencies, and the most important factor for this is motivation.

sections.label: AI, cognitive development and exports
sections.summary: Without this foundation AI may retard cognitive development, and Deputy Prime Minister Gan noted Singapore's exports could face higher duties if exemptions are not secured.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: Without this foundation, AI may only serve to retard the cognitive development instead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: I believe that the suggestions I have made in my speech will further strengthen us as a society and give all of our children a better chance to succeed in life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: As Deputy Prime Minister Gan noted earlier this week, if exemptions are not secured, Singapore's exports, such as pharmaceuticals to semiconductors to advanced manufacturing, could face higher duties.

sections.label: India AI investment ambitions
sections.summary: India has announced ambitions to attract up to US$200 billion in AI and data centre investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: India has announced ambitions to attract up to US$200 billion in AI and data centre investments.

sections.label: Anchoring AI in strong sectors
sections.summary: Anchoring AI in strong sectors like advanced manufacturing, aerospace, logistics, financial services and healthcare, then scaling to more sectors, creates higher value roles, resilient careers and wage growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: If we anchor AI in sectors where we are strong, such as mentioned, as advanced manufacturing, aerospace, logistics, financial services and healthcare, and scale to more sectors with measurable outcomes, we create higher value roles, more resilient careers and stronger wage growth.

sections.label: Pooled AI engineers and modules
sections.summary: Evolve CTO-as-a-service to AI-Capability-as-a-Service with pooled AI engineers for SME clusters, and pool industry resources to co-develop plug-and-play AI modules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: First, evolve CTO-as-a-service towards AI-Capability-as-a-Service with pooled AI engineers deployed across SME clusters for hands-on implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Second, organise pooled resources by industry to co-develop plug-and-play AI modules with industry leaders for generic processes, such as quality control, logistics optimisation and predictive maintenance.

sections.label: Outcome-linked co-funding
sections.summary: Introduce outcome-linked co-funding tied to measurable productivity, cost savings, export growth or energy efficiency, as shared by many Members of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Third, introduce outcome-linked co-funding tied to measurable productivity, cost savings, export growth or energy efficiency, something that was shared by many Members of Parliament yesterday.

sections.label: Gini, incomes and re-employment age
sections.summary: Post-tax-and-transfer Gini fell from about 0.47 in the mid-2000s to around 0.37 today, 20th percentile real incomes grew faster than the median, and the re-employment age rises to 70 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Our post-tax-and-transfer Gini coefficient has fallen from about 0.47 in the mid-2000s to around 0.37 today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Real incomes at the 20th percentile have grown faster than the median, supported by Workfare and the Progressive Wage Model and OECD studies indicate relatively strong intergenerational mobility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: For senior workers, the re-employment age will rise to 70 by 2030.

sections.label: Managers using AI tools
sections.summary: At a Chinese New Year conversation in Pasir Ris, some resident managers said they can now complete such tasks with AI tools themselves, reducing the need to hire and train fresh graduates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: At a recent Chinese New Year conversation in Pasir Ris, some of the residents were managers, told me that they can now complete such tasks with AI tools themselves, reducing the need to hire and train fresh graduates.

sections.label: AI for ageing at home
sections.summary: AI-enabled fall detection, smart home sensors, remote health monitoring and telemedicine can allow seniors to age safely at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: AI-enabled fall detection, smart home sensors, remote health monitoring and telemedicine can allow seniors to age safely at home.

sections.label: Wayfinding project for visually impaired
sections.summary: A trial used indoor positioning and AI image recognition to help visually impaired residents navigate complex indoor spaces, raising questions on scaling such projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Recently, I trialed a project with visually impaired residents to test a wayfinding solution using indoor positioning and AI image recognition to navigate complex indoor spaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: But how do we connect such projects to agencies, funding and testbeds and scale them with less friction?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: We may need a clearer pathway linking community innovators, GovTech, IMDA, healthcare institutions and social service agencies.

sections.label: AI goals for Singapore
sections.summary: AI must strengthen industries, uplift SMEs, empower seniors, open doors for graduates and protect the vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: AI must strengthen industries, uplift SMEs, empower seniors, open doors for graduates and protect the vulnerable, among many others.

sections.label: PARF rebate reduction and COE
sections.summary: The PARF rebate will be reduced by 45% and its cap lowered from $60,000 to $30,000 for COEs from February 2026's second bidding exercise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: As announced, the PARF rebate will be reduced by 45% and the cap lowered from $60,000 to $30,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: This change applies to Certificates of Entitlement (COEs) obtained from the second COE bidding exercise in February 2026 onwards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: My concern is the effective date and the absence of transition safeguards for buyers who had already committed to a car purchase under the prior framework.

sections.label: Concerns over PARF transition
sections.summary: Questions were raised on interim measures, relief for buyers who paid deposits before Budget Day, impact on car dealers, and COE renewals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: First, why was there no interim measures for buyers who had already committed and paid deposits before Budget Day, and would the revised PARF framework have started in a later COE cycle or with a longer lead time, so that the buyers have time to react and consider their decision to buy?

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Third, will the Government consider introducing a limited relief mechanism for buyers who entered into purchase agreements and paid deposits before Budget Day?

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Fourth, did the Government consider the impact on new-car sellers who typically commit to inventory and order pipelines six to 12 months in advance?

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: For these new car dealers, they are now at risk of holding stock that is much harder to sell and may have a knock-out effect on their business viability and also employees' jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Fifth, did the Government expect this change to increase COE renewals because retaining older cars becomes relatively more attractive and if so, what is the expected impact on the number of COEs available for the new cars and the resulting trajectory of the COE premiums?

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: For example, is the national power grid ready to support a mass adoption of EVs, and will EV charging, especially in older estates, keep in pace, so Singaporeans will not feel that policy is moving faster than practical realities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: But when the Government takes away value, it can be immediate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: I worry this perception would erode trust, especially if ordinary families are hurt because they are not sophisticated buyers and reasonably expect the rules to remain stable when making big purchases.

sections.label: Senior Employment Credit extension
sections.summary: Employers get a Senior Employment Credit, extended another year under this year's Budget, for seniors who wish to keep working.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If seniors wish to continue working, the Government provides employers with a Senior Employment Credit, which has been extended for another year under this year's Budget.

sections.label: Seniors living alone by 2030
sections.summary: The Ministerial Committee on Ageing estimates 83,000 seniors above 65 will live alone by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the Ministerial Committee on Ageing, an estimated 83,000 seniors above 65 years will live alone by the year 2030.

sections.label: Older adults' education levels
sections.summary: Population trends 2025 shows nearly 40% of those over 55 had below secondary education as at 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the Department of Statistics Population trends 2025, as at 2024, nearly 40% of those over 55 years old, have education at below secondary level – a very significant segment.

sections.label: Hougang HDB branch closure
sections.summary: Hougang Central HDB branch closed 1 September, leaving residents to travel to Sengkang, with counter services replaced by electronic and self-service machines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin): The HDB Branch Office at Hougang Central closed on 1 September, affecting areas, including Hougang Single Member Constituency and parts of Aljunied Group Representation Constituency (GRC).

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Residents told me that they now must travel to the more distant Sengkang Branch to do their business, which is very inconvenient.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Currently, HDB has not established a new physical branch nearby, but has replaced counter services with electronic service and self-service machines.

sections.label: Seniors' support and co-residence
sections.summary: A wage-earning adult child living with parents for mutual support may make seniors ineligible for or reduce their support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Should a wage-earning adult child decide to live with his or her parents for mutual support, the seniors may become ineligible for support or have support reduced compared to if they lived on their own.

sections.label: Per capita income criterion question
sections.summary: It asks whether the per capita household income criterion for schemes like Silver Support could be replaced by looking at seniors' own income.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would it be possible for instance, to do away with the per capita household income criterion for schemes, such as Silver Support, and simply look at the seniors' own income?

sections.label: Harmonised medical examination report scheme
sections.summary: Under the harmonised medical examination report scheme from 2 February, drivers attend one examination used by both agencies, with doctors uploading the report.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some have also had difficulties uploading the medical reports onto the portals of the two agencies, as they were not comfortable handling attachments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Now, under the new harmonised medical examination report scheme implemented on 2 February, drivers need only attend one medical examination that can be used by both agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In addition, the doctor will be the one uploading the medical report onto the relevant portal.

sections.label: Fertility support recommendations
sections.summary: Citing infertility statistics and low TFR, PAP Women's Wing MPs propose fertility screenings, ART subsidies, higher MediSave limits and related measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The struggles they face are deeply personal, often invisible and sometimes painful." SingHealth statistics indicate that roughly one in six couples, about 17%, experience infertility in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: FSS' community engagements reveal that financial costs are the top stressor, forcing some to abandon their fertility journey entirely.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: With two successive years of historically low TFR, Sir, the time to act is now.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
